Kindle Accessories: What Your Kindle Actually Needs

Facts checked October 5, 2026. Independent overview based on Amazon's user guides, listings and announcements plus press coverage, and on our detailed guides linked below. We have not tested the accessories mentioned.

Affiliate disclosure: Links to Amazon on this page are ordinary Amazon.com links. We are not Amazon and are not an authorized Amazon reseller. We may join the Amazon Associates program; if we do, qualifying links will carry a tracking tag and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you, and our disclosure page will say so. Our picks and wording are not paid for. Prices and specs change; the Amazon listing is the source of truth.

Search for Kindle accessories and you get hundreds of cases, pouches, stands, cables, remotes and gadgets, many of them labeled "for all Kindles." In practice, the right set depends on two things: which Kindle you own, down to its release year, and how you read. This page sorts accessories by the job they do, shows which ones apply to each model, and is honest about the things most readers can skip. Each section links to a detailed guide for the full answer.

Short answer

  • Most readers need one thing: protection for the screen in a bag. A folio cover that names your model and year, or a padded sleeve that is big enough.
  • Charging is probably covered. A cable comes in the box; check that it matches the port (USB-C or micro-USB) and use any safety-compliant USB adapter.
  • Everything else is situational: a stand for hands-free reading, a page turner if your Kindle sits out of reach, a dock if you own a Signature Edition that supports one.
  • Before buying anything, confirm your model and release year. It decides fit and compatibility more than the product name does.

Step one: know your Kindle

Almost every accessory mistake starts with the model name. "Kindle Paperwhite" has covered several different bodies since 2018, "Kindle Colorsoft" now means a 2024 model, a 2025 16 GB version, a redesigned 2026 model and a separate 11-inch Scribe Colorsoft, and the basic Kindle was redesigned again for 2026. Amazon's user guides say the Device Info screen in your Kindle's settings shows its name and generation, and the device list in your Amazon account shows the same. Write down the release year, because accessory listings and Amazon's own compatibility notes increasingly use it ("2024 release and onward") rather than a generation number.

If you are still deciding which Kindle to buy, settle that first: accessories bought for one generation rarely carry over. Our Paperwhite buying guide compares the 2026, 2024 and 2021 models.

Kindle accessories by need

Group accessories by the problem they solve and the list gets short. Here are the six jobs, what to look for in each, and where to read more.

Protection: cases and covers

A case or cover is the accessory most owners buy first, and the one where fit matters most, because it has to match the exact body: outer size, button position, port cutout and, on a folio, the magnet that wakes and sleeps the screen. The words "case" and "cover" are used loosely in listings, so think in constructions instead: a folio that closes over the screen, a back shell that leaves the screen open, or, for Amazon's 2026 aluminum models, a slim cover that attaches magnetically.

  • Check: your model and release year in the title; the power button and port cutouts; whether the folio wakes and sleeps the Kindle; how much weight it adds.
  • Signature Edition owners: thick or metal-backed cases can interfere with wireless charging on 2024-era models, and on the 2026 models a case must leave the pogo pins on the back clear if you want the dock or the Page-Turn Cover.
  • Read next: Kindle case buying guide for fit and styles; model guides for the Paperwhite, Scribe and Colorsoft; and Kindle covers explained if you are choosing between a flap and a shell.

Carrying: sleeves and pouches

A sleeve is a padded pouch you slide the Kindle into for the bag and take it out of to read. It adds nothing to the device in your hand and is less tied to one model than a case. The catch is sizing: "6-inch" or "7-inch" on a sleeve usually describes the screen it is meant for, not the pouch, and a few millimeters decide whether it fits.

  • Check: the stated interior dimensions against your Kindle's outer size (with any case on); padding on all sides; a zip or flap that closes fully; what "water-resistant" actually claims.
  • Read next: Kindle sleeve guide, including a size table by model.

Reading position: stands and holders

A stand is for reading without holding the Kindle: at a desk while eating, on a treadmill shelf, or in bed. Desk stands, gooseneck holders, pillow stands and Amazon's own docks solve different problems. Many folio covers fold into a basic stand, so check whether the cover you already own does the job before buying a separate one.

  • Check: stability with your Kindle's weight and case; angle adjustment; whether the holder grips a Kindle with its case on; for a dock, exactly which models it lists.
  • Read next: Kindle stand guide and its dock section.

Charging: cables, adapters and docks

The charging question is mostly about the connector. Kindles from the 2021 Paperwhite onward that we checked use USB-C; older models such as the 2018 Paperwhite, 2019 Kindle, Oasis and Voyage use micro-USB. Amazon's user guides quote charge times with its own 5W or 9W adapters and also give times for third-party adapters and computer ports, so a reputable, safety-compliant adapter you already own will work, typically more slowly than the quoted figure.

  • Check: USB-C or micro-USB; a recognized safety mark on any adapter; for wireless charging, that your model supports it at all (only some Signature Editions do, and the 2026 Signature Editions use a pogo-pin dock instead of Qi).
  • Read next: Kindle charger guide, with a port table by model and charging troubleshooting.

Page turning: remotes, buttons and tappers

For years Amazon did not support Bluetooth page-turn remotes on Kindle e-readers, so third-party makers sold clip-on gadgets that physically tap the screen. On October 1, 2026 Amazon announced its own Kindle Click remote and a Page-Turn Cover with physical buttons. Which option applies depends almost entirely on your Kindle's release year.

  • Check: release year first (the Click is listed for 2024 and later); whether you need back as well as forward; for clip-ons, where the receiver sits on the screen and whether it grips over your case.
  • Free options first: Signature Editions from 2024 on have Double Tap in their user guides or Amazon's announcement, and every Kindle has large tap zones for one-handed reading.
  • Read next: Kindle page turner guide, starting with what each Kindle supports.

By model: start from the device

If you are buying a Kindle and accessories together, choose the device first and then follow its accessory list. Our Paperwhite guide covers the 2026 Signature Edition's pogo-pin features and what they mean for docks and covers. For the large writing tablets, the Scribe case guide explains why pen storage changes the choice of case. The matrix below puts it all in one place.

Two patterns stand out. First, the 2024 release year is a dividing line for page turning, because that is how Amazon words the Kindle Click's compatibility. Second, Signature Editions have the most accessory-specific features, and those features changed in 2026: the 2021 and 2024 Paperwhite Signature Editions and the 2024 Colorsoft Signature Edition support Qi wireless charging, while the 2026 Signature Editions drop Qi in favor of pogo pins, according to The Verge. A dock or case made for one generation is not a safe bet for the other.

What you may not need to buy

Accessory listings are good at suggesting problems you do not have. These are the purchases we would question first, based on what Amazon documents.

  • A "Kindle charger" bundle, if you already have a USB wall adapter and the cable from the box. Amazon's guides give charge times for third-party adapters; what matters is a safety-compliant adapter and the right connector.
  • A wireless charging pad, unless you own a Signature Edition that supports Qi. Standard models do not, the 2026 Signature Editions do not, and Amazon's user guides list Qi-certified chargers that do not work with the 2024 Signature Editions because of mechanical incompatibility.
  • A generic Bluetooth remote for an older Kindle. Amazon says Kindle e-readers do not support pairing Bluetooth keyboards or mice, and its Kindle Click is listed as not compatible with Kindles launched before 2024. On those models, a clip-on tapper or a better reading position is the realistic route.
  • A clip-on book light. Every Paperwhite and Colorsoft has a built-in front light (Amazon and WIRED describe adjustable warm light on the 2026 models), and so do the Oasis and the basic Kindles from 2019 to 2024 we checked. The exceptions are older basic Kindles and the 2025 Kindle Scribe that Amazon sells without a front light; for those, a light can make sense.
  • A screen protector under a folio. If a cover already closes over the screen, a protector adds little for most readers, and we found no tests of how protectors affect the Colorsoft's color layer. It is more defensible on a bare Kindle or one in a back shell.
  • Both a heavy case and a padded sleeve. Pick the one that matches where the risk is. A thin cover plus a sleeve can make sense; a rugged case inside a padded pouch is usually redundant.
  • A stylus for a non-Scribe Kindle. Writing with a pen is a Scribe feature; the other Kindles are designed for touch.
  • Anything marketed as "official" or "Amazon certified" that is not sold under Amazon's own brand. We cannot verify those claims, and they are not a reason to pay more.

A sensible buying order

  1. Identify your Kindle and its release year from Device Info or your Amazon account.
  2. Choose protection for how you carry it: a model-specific cover or case, or a sleeve sized from the interior dimensions.
  3. Check what you already have for charging: the cable that came in the box and any reputable USB adapter. Buy a spare cable of the right connector only if you need one in another room or bag.
  4. Add comfort items after a few weeks of reading, when you know whether you actually want a stand, a dock or a page turner.
  5. Keep the receipts. With third-party fit and compatibility often unverified, an easy return window is worth more than a small discount.

How we put this together

This page summarizes our detailed guides rather than repeating them, and each guide lists its own sources. The compatibility statements here come from Amazon's user guides (port labels, charge times, Qi support and incompatible chargers, Double Tap, Device Info), Amazon's help page on pairing Bluetooth devices with a Kindle, Amazon.com listings for the Kindle Click and Amazon's docks, Amazon's October 1, 2026 lineup announcement, and coverage from The Verge and WIRED. We have not tested any accessory and we do not rank third-party products. Prices are those Amazon announced or listed as of October 5, 2026 and will change. To report a mistake, use our contact page; our approach is described in the editorial policy.

Frequently asked questions

What Kindle accessories do I actually need?

For most people, one: something that protects the screen when the Kindle is in a bag. That can be a folio cover that fits your model year or a padded sleeve. Your Kindle comes with a charging cable, and Amazon's user guides say any safety-compliant USB adapter or computer port will charge it, so a wall adapter you already own usually covers charging. Stands, docks and page turners are about comfort, not need. Start with protection, then add others only if a specific situation calls for them.

Do Kindle accessories work across models?

Some do and some do not. Cases and covers are tied to the exact body, so they depend on the model and release year, not just the name. Cables depend on the port: USB-C on the 2021 Paperwhite, the 2022 Kindle and newer models we checked, micro-USB on older ones such as the Oasis, the 2019 Kindle and the 2018 Paperwhite. Amazon's Kindle Click remote works only with Kindles released in 2024 or later, and the Page-Turn Cover and the new pogo-pin dock are limited to the 2026 Paperwhite and Colorsoft Signature Editions. Sleeves and stands are the most forgiving, as long as the size suits. See the model matrix.

How do I find out which Kindle model I have?

Amazon's user guides say the Device Info screen in the Kindle's settings shows the device's name and generation, and the device list in your Amazon account (Manage Your Content and Devices) shows the same. Match accessories by release year where the listing gives one, because generation numbers are used inconsistently across listings. Our Paperwhite, Scribe and Colorsoft guides also describe what each model looks like.

Is a case or a sleeve better for a Kindle?

It depends on where the risk is. A case or folio stays on while you read, so it protects against drops at home and on the move, at the cost of weight and a model-specific fit. A sleeve protects only while the Kindle is inside it, but it adds nothing to the device in your hand and can outlast a device upgrade if the size still works. Some people use both: a thin cover for reading and a sleeve in the bag. The sleeve vs case comparison goes into detail.

Do I need a special Kindle charger?

Usually not. Amazon sells its own adapters and quotes its fastest charge times with them, but its user guides also give charge times for third-party adapters and computer ports, and tell owners to use a charger or port that complies with safety standards. The main thing to get right is the cable connector, USB-C or micro-USB. Wireless charging is limited to some Signature Editions. The charger guide lists the port and Amazon's stated charge times for each model.

Can I use a Bluetooth page turner with my Kindle?

Amazon's own Kindle Click remote is listed as compatible with Kindles released in 2024 or later, and Amazon says it is not compatible with earlier models. For older Kindles, Amazon's help page says pairing a Bluetooth keyboard or mouse is not supported, which is why clip-on tappers that physically tap the screen are sold. Whether third-party Bluetooth remotes work on 2024 and newer Kindles is not something Amazon documents. Details are in the page turner guide.

Are Amazon's own Kindle accessories better than third-party ones?

They are the ones Amazon documents. For example, Amazon says the 2024 Colorsoft's Double Tap feature was tested with Amazon's own Colorsoft case and may not work with all third-party cases, and Amazon's docks list exactly which models they fit. Third-party accessories are often cheaper and more varied. We have not tested accessories from either source, so we do not rank them. Wording such as "official" or "Amazon certified" on a non-Amazon product is something we cannot verify.

Do accessories for the new 2026 Kindles exist yet?

Amazon announced its own on October 1, 2026: Kindle Covers from $39.99, slim magnetic-attach covers for the aluminum models, the $79.99 Page-Turn Cover and a $59.99 Charging Dock for the Paperwhite and Colorsoft Signature Editions, and the $34.99 Kindle Click. As of October 5, 2026 the 2026 Paperwhite and Colorsoft had not shipped (Amazon gives October 28, 2026), so third-party cases for them could not yet be checked against real devices. Older cases will not fit: the 2026 bodies are thinner and the power button has moved.

Kindle Paperwhite: Which One Should You Buy in 2026?

Facts checked October 2, 2026 against Amazon's announcement and listings and launch coverage from WIRED, The Verge, TechRadar and Engadget. Independent buying guide, not affiliated with Amazon.

Affiliate disclosure: Links to Amazon on this page are ordinary Amazon.com links. We are not Amazon and are not an authorized Amazon reseller. We may join the Amazon Associates program; if we do, qualifying links will carry a tracking tag and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you, and our disclosure page will say so. Our picks and wording are not paid for. Prices and specs change; the Amazon listing is the source of truth.

The Kindle Paperwhite is the one most people end up buying: a 7-inch glare-free screen, an adjustable warm front light, waterproofing, and battery life measured in weeks. The tricky part right now is timing. Amazon just announced a redesigned Paperwhite, the 2024 model is still on sale, and the 2021 model is what a lot of people still own. This page sorts out what changed, what did not, and which one makes sense for you.

The short answer

  • Want a Paperwhite right now? The 2024 model (12th generation) is the one that is shipping and fully reviewed. Amazon lists it at $199.99 today. See the 2024 Kindle Paperwhite (16 GB) on Amazon.
  • Can wait until late October? The 2026 Paperwhite ships October 28 at the same starting prices ($199.99 / $249.99 Signature). It is thinner and lighter with the same rated battery life. Wait for the first independent reviews before you pre-order if you are cautious.
  • Own the 2021 Paperwhite and it works? Upgrading is a comfort and speed decision, not a necessity. Plenty of readers will not notice enough to justify $200.
  • Buying a case? Fit is model-year specific. See our Kindle Paperwhite case guide by model year and the general Kindle case guide before you order anything.

Notice the price line. The 2024 Paperwhite launched at $159.99 and is now $199.99, and the new model starts at the same $199.99. WIRED reports that Amazon raised prices on existing Kindles earlier this year and cites memory costs as the reason. In other words, you are not paying a premium for the new model over the old one right now. Whether that stays true once retailers start discounting the 2024 version is something only time will answer.

What is new in the 2026 Paperwhite

Amazon's announcement describes a redesigned family rather than a new display. Here is what is actually different, based on the announcement and launch coverage:

  • Thinner and lighter. WIRED lists the new Paperwhite at 6.8 mm and 204 g, versus 7.8 mm and 211 g for the 2024 model. That is a millimeter and a few grams. You will feel the thickness more than the weight.
  • Flush-front, edge-to-edge look. Amazon says it built a new "reverse stack" display construction across the whole lineup, with no raised border interrupting the reading surface, and device color that wraps from the front to the back.
  • Oxide TFT backplane. Amazon says the Paperwhite uses an oxide thin-film transistor backplane and has its highest contrast ratio yet. The Verge notes the core display specs, such as size, did not change.
  • Power button moved. Every new Kindle now has the power button on the right edge near the top instead of the bottom. This is the kind of detail that makes old cases a poor bet.
  • User-replaceable battery. The Verge reports Amazon says the new Kindles have user-replaceable batteries to comply with EU rules. Treat that as a nice-to-have, not something to plan around.
  • New colors and a metal option. The standard Paperwhite comes in Graphite. The Signature Edition is aluminum, in Graphite and Seaglass Green.

What did not change is just as important. The screen size is still 7 inches, the advertised battery life is still up to 12 weeks, it is still waterproof, and the starting price is the same. If you were hoping for a color screen on the Paperwhite, that is still the Colorsoft's job.

A note on trust

The new Paperwhite had not shipped when we checked, and we have no hands-on time with it. Everything above comes from Amazon's announcement and from journalists who handled pre-release units. We will not claim the new screen "looks better" or the page turns are "faster" than the 2024 model, because we do not know yet, and the one speed figure Amazon initially gave to press was corrected after publication.

Should you wait?

Think of it as three scenarios. If you are buying a gift for the next two weeks, the 2024 model is the safe choice because it exists and has been reviewed to death. If you are buying for yourself and can wait four weeks, wait: the new one costs the same on paper, is slimmer, and you will get to read real reviews before spending. If you are a bargain hunter, keep an eye on the 2024 model's price once the new one ships. Retailers often clear previous-generation stock, but we are not going to promise a discount we cannot see.

One more consideration is accessories. A new body means new cases. If you already own a case, a dock, or a wireless charger for a 2024 Paperwhite, factor in that some of it may not work with the 2026 one. The Signature Edition, for instance, trades wireless charging for pogo pins. That is a reason to stay on the 2024 model if you have invested in Qi chargers.

Signature Edition vs standard

The Signature Edition has been the premium Paperwhite since 2021, and the extras have shifted a little each generation. The things that have stayed constant are 32 GB of storage and an auto-adjusting front light, plus a no-ads lock screen. The pricing gap has also been steady: roughly $50 over the standard model.

  • Storage: 32 GB versus 16 GB on the current models. For ordinary ebooks, 16 GB is plenty (Amazon says thousands of books). It matters if you keep a lot of audiobooks, comics or large PDFs on the device. TechRadar notes the operating system uses a chunk of the 16 GB, so the usable figure is lower.
  • Auto-adjusting front light: a sensor changes brightness for you. Some readers love it; others turn it off and set a schedule instead.
  • Charging: wireless on the 2024 Signature Edition; pogo-pin dock on the 2026 one.
  • Build: plastic in 2024, aluminum in 2026.

The honest value test: if you read mostly novels and rarely use audiobooks on the device, the standard model does the job and the $50 difference is better spent on a decent case. If you want the best build, no ads, and you do not want to think about brightness at night, the Signature Edition is the one to pick.

Ads, storage and the "which version" trap

The Kindle product pages are a maze of near-identical listings. A few habits keep you out of trouble.

  1. Check the ad status. Lock screen ads are sold as an option on standard Kindles. When the 2024 Paperwhite launched, Amazon priced the ad-free version $20 higher ($159.99 with ads, $179.99 without). WIRED's 2026 rundown lists the plastic Paperwhite as having lock screen ads and the aluminum Signature Edition as having none.
  2. Check the storage. The standard and Signature Editions are different SKUs. Make sure the capacity in the title is the one you want.
  3. Check the color. The 2024 model came in Black, Raspberry and Jade; the Signature Edition in Metallic versions of those. The 2026 lineup has different colors, and the standard model is Graphite only at launch.
  4. Check the seller. A listing shipped and sold by Amazon.com is the simplest for returns and warranty. Amazon's 2024 listing mentions a 1-year limited warranty and a 30-day refund and replacement window; confirm the terms on the listing you buy from.

Paperwhite vs Kindle, Colorsoft and Scribe

The Paperwhite sits in the middle of the range. Here is how it compares with the others on Amazon's own comparison table (as of October 2, 2026), plus the 2026 refresh of the base Kindle and Colorsoft.

The 2026 refresh pushes the base Kindle to 140 g and 6.8 mm with 30% faster book opening (per Amazon), and adds a 32 GB aluminum version at $189.99. WIRED and The Verge both point out that this puts the aluminum base Kindle close to the Paperwhite's price once you add a cover, and the Paperwhite is the one with the denser, auto-dimming screen. If you have narrowed it to "Paperwhite or plain Kindle," the Paperwhite is usually worth the extra $50. If it is "Paperwhite or Colorsoft," ask yourself honestly how much of what you read has color.

Who should buy which

Commuters and travelers

Anything in the Paperwhite family. The size is the draw: bigger than a phone, smaller than a paperback. The 2026 model's lower weight and thickness are an advantage if you carry it in a small bag all day, though a 1 mm difference will not change your life.

Bedtime readers

The warm light is the main event here, and every Paperwhite has it. The Signature Edition's automatic light adjustment saves you from fiddling at night. Pair it with a case that wraps the back and edges so the device does not slip off the pillow.

Pool, beach and bath readers

All Paperwhites listed here are waterproof. Be sensible: Amazon's rating is for fresh water, and a case that holds water against the device will make it slower to dry. See our case guide's water section.

Students and people with big PDFs

A 7-inch screen is better than 6 for PDFs, but it is still not a document reader. If you annotate heavily, look at the Scribe; if you mostly read novels with the occasional PDF, the Paperwhite is fine.

Gift buyers

Standard Paperwhite plus a good case is the default answer. Check the ad status and, if the recipient reads in bed, consider the Signature Edition's auto light. Our case guide has what to avoid when buying for a model you cannot hold.

Before you buy: a short checklist

  • Confirm the model year on the listing and in your cart.
  • Decide on 16 GB vs 32 GB. If you do not use audiobooks or comics on the device, 16 GB is enough.
  • Decide whether ads on the lock screen bother you.
  • Check the exact color and finish you want, and that it is the one in stock.
  • Plan the case before you buy the device, not after.
  • Read the rated battery conditions: half an hour a day, wireless off, light at 13. Your use may differ.
  • Check the return window and warranty on the listing.

Accessories to plan for

The case is the accessory that matters most, and the one where model-year mismatches cost people money. Amazon's 2026 accessories include covers from $39.99 in knit fabric, plant-based leather and pebbled leather; a Page-Turn Cover at $79.99 for the Signature Edition; a $59.99 charging dock for the Signature Edition; and the $34.99 Kindle Click Bluetooth remote, which Amazon says works with all new Kindles and any Kindle from 2024 or later.

The Kindle Click is the interesting one if you like physical page-turn buttons but do not want to upgrade, since it works with the 2024 Paperwhite too; our Kindle page turner guide compares it with the alternatives. If you want a Kindle you can write on instead, the Scribe has its own set of cases; see our Kindle Scribe case guide.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a new Kindle Paperwhite in 2026?

Yes. Amazon announced a redesigned Kindle Paperwhite on October 1, 2026. It is available to pre-order and is scheduled to ship October 28, 2026. It is thinner and lighter than the 2024 model, keeps the 7-inch size and up to 12 weeks of rated battery life, and starts at $199.99 (16 GB) with a $249.99 Signature Edition (32 GB, aluminum back). Because it has not shipped, independent hands-on reviews were not yet available when this page was written.

Should I buy the 2024 Kindle Paperwhite or wait for the 2026 one?

If both are the same price when you check, the newer one is the better long-term pick on paper: it is about 1 mm thinner and a few grams lighter, with the same advertised battery life. If you need a Kindle this week, the 2024 model is a well-reviewed, fully tested device. If you find the 2024 model discounted, the savings can easily outweigh the 2026 refinements, which are mostly physical rather than a leap in reading quality.

What is the difference between the Kindle Paperwhite and the Signature Edition?

Across generations the Signature Edition adds 32 GB of storage, an auto-adjusting front light, and a premium finish, and drops lock screen ads. On the 2024 model it also added wireless charging. On the 2026 model Amazon lists an aluminum rear housing, double-tap page turns, and pogo-pin dock charging instead; news coverage says wireless charging is not offered on the new Signature Edition. See the Signature section.

Is the Kindle Paperwhite waterproof?

The 2024 Paperwhite has an IPX8 rating: Amazon says it is tested to withstand immersion in 2 meters of fresh water for 60 minutes. That is a fresh-water test; it does not mean you should drop it in the ocean or a hot tub. Amazon describes the 2026 model as waterproof as well, but check the rating on the final product listing.

How long does the Paperwhite battery last?

Amazon rates both the 2024 and 2026 models at up to 12 weeks. That figure is based on 30 minutes of reading per day with wireless off and the light at setting 13. If you read for hours daily, use a bright front light, or stream audiobooks over Bluetooth, expect to charge more often.

Does the Kindle Paperwhite come with ads?

Standard Paperwhites are sold with lock screen ads unless the listing says otherwise; WIRED's launch report says the plastic 2026 Paperwhite has lock screen ads and the Signature Edition does not. When the 2024 model launched, Amazon charged $20 more for an ad-free version, so check which version the listing you are on actually sells.

Will my old Kindle Paperwhite case fit the new model?

Do not assume so. Amazon's own cover for the 2024 Paperwhite is listed as fitting the 2024 release only, and the 2021 and 2024 bodies differ in width, height and thickness. The 2026 body is thinner again and has a moved power button. Buy only a case whose listing explicitly names your model year. More on this in our Paperwhite case guide by model year and the general Kindle case guide.

Can I read EPUB files on a Kindle Paperwhite?

Per Amazon's 2024 listing, the Paperwhite natively handles AZW3, AZW, TXT, PDF, unprotected MOBI and PRC, and supports formats such as EPUB, DOCX, HTML and image files through conversion (for example via Amazon's send-to-Kindle tools). Library and store-bought books with DRM from other retailers will not simply open on a Kindle.

Which Kindle is best for most people?

For most readers who want a sharp screen, a warm light and waterproofing, the Paperwhite is the sensible middle of the lineup. The base 6-inch Kindle is cheaper and smaller but has a shorter rated battery life (up to 6 weeks). The Colorsoft costs more and is mainly for people who want color for covers, comics, or graphic content.

Kindle Case Buying Guide: Fit First, Style Second

Facts checked October 2, 2026. Independent guide based on Amazon listings and launch coverage; we have not hands-on tested every case mentioned.

Affiliate disclosure: Links to Amazon on this page are ordinary Amazon.com links. We are not Amazon and are not an authorized Amazon reseller. We may join the Amazon Associates program; if we do, qualifying links will carry a tracking tag and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you, and our disclosure page will say so. Buying a Kindle case should be easy, and it mostly is, as long as you get one thing right: the model year. The most common reason a case ends up in a drawer is that it was made for a different generation. This guide shows how to avoid that, how the main styles compare, and what to check before you order, with extra attention to the brand-new 2026 Paperwhite, which almost certainly will not fit cases made for the one before.

The short answer

  1. Match the exact model year named in the listing to your Kindle. If it does not name one, move on.
  2. Pick the style by how you read: a magnetic folio for most people, a slim shell if you hate bulk, a stand or strap case for hands-free or one-handed reading, a sleeve if the Kindle just lives in a bag. Not sure whether you want a flap or a shell? See Kindle covers explained.
  3. Check the cutouts and charging (power button, USB-C) and whether it has auto sleep/wake.
  4. On the 2026 Paperwhite? Buy only a case that explicitly names the 2026 model, or Amazon's own covers (from $39.99).

Need help choosing the Kindle first? See our Kindle Paperwhite buying guide. Own a Paperwhite? Our Kindle Paperwhite case guide sorts cases by 2026, 2024, 2021 and older models, and our Kindle Scribe case guide covers the 10.2-inch and 11-inch Scribes and where the pen goes.

Fit: why model year matters

Amazon sells devices called "Kindle Paperwhite" in several sizes. They share a name and a general shape, but not dimensions, and a case cut for one will pinch, gap or block the buttons on another. Here is what the published numbers say:

Dimensions and weights from Amazon's 2024 listing, PCWorld's 2021 review, and WIRED's Oct 1, 2026 launch report. The 2026 width and height were not in the sources we checked.
ModelScreenSize (W × H × D)WeightNotes that affect fit

Paperwhite 2026 (new)7-inchThickness 6.8 mm; width and height not confirmed in our sources204 gPower button moved to the right edge; new covers announced

Between 2021 and 2024 the device grew about 3 mm wider and 1.5 mm taller while getting 0.3 mm thinner. That sounds trivial until you try to snap a hard shell on, where a millimeter is the difference between a tight fit and a case that will not close. That is why even the manufacturer's own 2024 cover is described as fitting the 2024 release only.

Before you order, find your model. The listing title should say something like "Kindle Paperwhite 12th generation, 2024 release" or "7-inch." If it says "fits all Kindle Paperwhite," treat it as a warning, not a feature. Check your device's information screen and your Amazon account's device list for the generation; Amazon's help pages explain how to identify any model.

If you own a Paperwhite, our Kindle Paperwhite case guide goes through each model year in detail. One practical note: several 2024 Paperwhite case listings also name the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition, since the two share a body. If you own a Colorsoft, a case listed for it works the same as above; just verify the listing names your exact model. Our Kindle Colorsoft case guide sorts the 2024, 2025 and 2026 Colorsoft models and the color-screen questions. The Scribe is a different case: it is much larger and its pen needs a place to live, so see our Kindle Scribe case guide.

Materials

Fabric

Fabric covers, such as the knit options Amazon announced for 2026, tend to be light, soft and friendly to humid hands. Amazon's fabric cover for the 2024 Paperwhite is described as made from recycled polyester and "water-safe." The tradeoff is that fabric may offer less rigid protection against a corner impact than a hardback.

Synthetic ("PU") leather

The most common material in third-party cases. It looks good, wipes clean, and is cheap to make. Quality varies a lot, from nicely finished to flaky and smelly. Listings usually combine PU leather with a microfiber lining to protect the screen, and a hard plastic shell inside.

Plant-based and premium leather

Amazon sells plant-based leather and, for 2026, pebbled premium leather covers. These sit at the top of the price range, with 2026 Amazon covers starting at $39.99. If you want a cover that looks better as it ages, this is where to look, but weigh the added cost against the Kindle's own price.

Hard plastic and TPU

Shells use polycarbonate or flexible TPU. They add grip and edge protection with little weight. Clear versions show off the Kindle's color, which matters more in 2026, since Amazon is making a point of color wrapping around the body.

Features that matter

  • Auto wake/sleep. A magnet in the cover signals the Kindle to wake when opened and sleep when closed. Amazon describes its covers as doing exactly that. It is a genuinely useful convenience, and any decent folio should have it.
  • Cutouts. Power button and USB-C port should be clear. On the 2026 models the power button is on the right edge near the top, so a case that places it at the bottom is the wrong one.
  • Charging with the case on. Look for a precise USB-C cutout. If you plan to use a dock or wireless charger, check compatibility explicitly, since the 2024 Signature Edition used Qi and the 2026 one uses pogo pins. Our Kindle charger guide lists the port and charging options for each model.
  • Fold-back design. A cover that folds fully back lets you read one-handed without a flap in the way. Some cases add a hand strap, which helps in bed and on a train.
  • Weight. A new Paperwhite weighs about 204 to 214 g depending on the model; a cover adds to that. Some Amazon reviewers say an official cover makes the device feel noticeably heavier. If weight matters, choose slim.
  • Stand. Useful for tables and flights, but adds bulk. A separate stand or dock is a different purchase; see our Kindle stand guide.
  • Card slots. A few listings add them. Handy if you want a one-piece carry, but they thicken the case.

Water, sand and the Paperwhite's waterproofing

The 2024 Paperwhite is rated IPX8, tested by Amazon at 2 meters of fresh water for 60 minutes, so a case is not needed for splashes. If you read by the pool, a case can still make sense for grip and for keeping sunscreen off the device, but think about drying. A case that traps water against the screen and ports will make cleanup slower, and leatherette can stain. Amazon markets its fabric cover as water-safe for exactly this reason. Rinse and dry any cover after contact with chlorine or salt water, and note that IPX8 is a fresh-water rating.

Amazon covers vs third-party cases

Amazon's own covers have an advantage that is easy to overlook: they are designed to the final specification and sold with a named model in the title. For 2026, Amazon lists covers from $39.99 in knit fabric, plant-based leather and pebbled leather that wrap fully around the device, slim magnetic-attach covers for aluminum models, and a Page-Turn Cover ($79.99) with physical buttons for the Paperwhite Signature Edition and Colorsoft Signature Edition.

Third-party cases dominate Amazon's results for the 2024 Paperwhite. Examples we saw in a search for "case covers for kindle paperwhite 2024" were Fintie, Moko, TNP and CoBak. We name them only so you know what the listings look like; we are not recommending or ranking them, and we have not tested them. Typical selling points are PU leather, magnetic closure, auto wake/sleep, a hardback shell, stands, hand straps and card slots, usually at a lower price than Amazon's covers.

Our rule of thumb: for a new device, wait for the manufacturer's cover or a third-party listing that names the exact model. For a device that has been on sale for a year or more, third-party cases are mature and varied. Read the reviews that mention fit and button cutouts, and sort by recent.

Search Amazon: 2024 Paperwhite cases

Buying for the new 2026 Paperwhite

The 2026 Paperwhite ships October 28, 2026. Here is how we would handle cases:

  • Do not buy a 2024 case "just in case." The body is a different thickness (6.8 mm vs 7.8 mm), the power button has moved, and Amazon's own cover for the old model is explicitly for the 2024 release only.
  • Look for the model name in the title. For the first few weeks, listings from sellers who have not seen the final device can be guesswork. Prioritize those with reviews from buyers who have received the device.
  • Consider Amazon's covers first. They start at $39.99 and are announced for the full lineup, with slim magnetic-attach versions for the aluminum Signature Edition.
  • Signature Edition owners: there are pogo pins on the back for the $79.99 Page-Turn Cover and the $59.99 charging dock. A third-party case that blocks them will block those accessories.
  • Want page-turn buttons without a special case? The Kindle Click is a $34.99 Bluetooth remote that Amazon says works with all new Kindles and any Kindle from 2024 or later. Our Kindle page turner guide compares it with the other options.

For the device itself, see 2026 vs 2024 compared; for what we know about 2026 cases, see the 2026 Paperwhite case section.

Listing red flags

  • No model year or generation in the title. If the listing only says "fits Kindle Paperwhite," keep scrolling.
  • "Fits 6-inch, 6.8-inch and 7-inch." No single hard case fits that range well.
  • Reviews mention the wrong size. Sort by most recent and search for "fit" and "too tight."
  • Stock photos of the wrong device. Does the image show a power button in the right place for your model?
  • Prices far under similar listings. Possible, but check the material and the reviews.
  • Claims of "official" or "Amazon certified." Be wary of wording that implies endorsement. A third-party case is a third-party case. We use no such language on this site either.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a case for my Kindle?

Not strictly. Kindles are built to be used bare, and the Paperwhite is waterproof. A case helps with scratches in a bag, grip, and comfort, and many people like the auto sleep/wake that a magnetic folio provides. If your Kindle lives at home, you can skip it. If it travels in a backpack, get something.

How do I know which case fits my Kindle?

Match the model year and screen size, not just the name. "Kindle Paperwhite" has been several different sizes. The 2021 Paperwhite is 6.8 inches and 124.6 × 175.2 × 8.1 mm; the 2024 model is 7 inches and 127.6 × 176.7 × 7.8 mm; the 2026 model is thinner again at 6.8 mm. A listing that names your exact model year and generation is the one to buy. See the fit section.

Will a 2024 Paperwhite case fit the new 2026 Paperwhite?

Assume no until a listing says it does. Amazon's own cover for the 2024 model is listed as fitting the 2024 release only, and the 2026 body is a different shape: thinner, with the power button moved to the right edge. Amazon says its new 2026 covers wrap fully around the device. Wait for listings that explicitly name the 2026 model.

Can I charge my Kindle with the case on?

Most folio and shell cases have a USB-C cutout, and Amazon's own fabric cover for the 2024 Paperwhite is described as able to remain on the device while charging. Check the listing for a charging-port cutout. Wireless charging through a thick case or a case with a metal plate or magnet layout may not work, and the 2026 Signature Edition uses pogo-pin charging rather than Qi, so check that too.

Is a leather or fabric case better?

Neither is better in every situation. Fabric is typically lighter and friendlier to damp hands; synthetic or plant-based leather feels more premium and wipes clean but can be heavier. Genuine leather is rare at lower prices. What matters more is fit, weight and whether the cover folds back flat for one-handed reading.

Do magnetic covers hurt the Kindle?

The wake/sleep feature in Kindle covers is designed around a small magnet in the cover, and Amazon sells magnetic covers itself. Normal use is fine. Just keep the Kindle away from strong magnets and do not store it with cards or items you do not want near a magnet.

What about a case for a Kindle Colorsoft or a base Kindle?

The same rules apply: model year first. Several 2024 Paperwhite case listings also name the Colorsoft Signature Edition because the bodies are shared, but verify on the listing. The base 6-inch Kindle is a different size and has been redesigned for 2026.

Should I buy a screen protector as well?

Optional. If you already have a folio cover that closes over the screen, a screen protector adds little. If you use a shell or a bare Kindle in a bag, a protector made specifically for your model can help against scratches, but choose one that does not add glare or reduce touch response, and read reviews.

Step 1: Identify your Paperwhite

People often describe their device as "my Paperwhite" or "the one from a few years ago," and then buy a case by name. Start instead from what you can see. Screen size and power button position are enough to separate the recent models:

  • 6-inch screen, flush front, power button on the bottom edge: the 2018 model (10th generation).
  • 6.8-inch screen, power button on the bottom edge: the 2021 model (11th generation), including its Signature Edition.
  • 7-inch screen, power button on the bottom edge: the 2024 model (12th generation).
  • 7-inch screen, power button on the right edge near the top: the new 2026 model.

For certainty, check the device information in Settings and the device list in your Amazon account, then match it to the "Generation" and "release" lines in the listing. Amazon's 2024 listing, for example, reads "Kindle Paperwhite (12th Generation) - 2024 release," and its 2018 technical sheet reads "10th Generation – 2018 release." A case listing should use the same wording. (Own a Kindle Scribe instead? It is a different, much larger device with a pen; see our Kindle Scribe case guide. Looking at Colorsoft? See Kindle Colorsoft case.)

This is still the model with the most third-party choice today. It is 7-inch, 127.6 × 176.7 × 7.8 mm and 211 g, with the power button on the bottom edge. It can stay on while charging, per the same listings.

Third-party cases dominate Amazon's results for this model, and the common selling points are PU leather, magnetic closure, auto sleep/wake, a hardback shell, a stand, a hand strap and card slots. Prices are generally lower than Amazon's covers, and because the model has been on sale for a while, you can read reviews that mention fit and cutouts. Sort by most recent, then search the reviews for "fit," "tight," "button" and "charging."

Two things to watch. First, several 2024 Paperwhite listings also name the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition because the bodies are shared; that is fine if you own one, but the listing should name your exact model (our Kindle Colorsoft case guide covers the Colorsoft models separately). Second, this is the model most affected by the 2026 launch: some sellers may relabel or add the new model to an existing listing without checking, so make sure the title and the recent reviews agree. Published heights differ by a millimeter between sources (174.2 mm in some spec tables, 175.2 mm in PCWorld's review), another reminder that listings should name the generation instead of the dimensions.

Amazon's launch announcement mentioned leather, cork and fabric covers for the model, and Amazon's current fabric cover listing for it says the cover is for the 11th generation Paperwhite and Signature Edition and "will not fit prior generation Kindle devices." Third-party cases for 6.8-inch Paperwhites remain easy to find. The main trap is the near-identical 2024 listings: a case marked "6.8-inch" is for 2021, and one marked "7-inch" is for 2024. If a listing claims to fit both, be skeptical, since hard cases are cut to a single body.

If you own a 2021 Paperwhite and are thinking of upgrading, bear in mind that a new device means a new case. A good case on a working 2021 Kindle is cheaper than a new Kindle.

The 2018 Paperwhite (10th generation) is a 6-inch device, 167 × 116 × 8.18 mm and 182 g for the Wi-Fi model, and was the first Paperwhite rated IPX8. Cases for it are still sold, usually titled "10th Generation, 2018 release" or "6-inch." Paperwhites released before 2018 had a raised bezel rather than a flush front, and CNET noted the 2015 model shared its chassis with the 2013 one. They need cases designed for that body, and many listings are old and unreliable. If you have one, look for a case that names your exact generation and matches the ten-year-old shape, or consider whether upgrading makes more sense than a new accessory. In every older case, buy from a seller with a clear return window.

Travel and wet weather

IPX8 on the Paperwhite is about the device surviving fresh-water immersion for a rated time and depth. A case answers different travel jobs: keeping the screen from keys in a backpack, giving you a grip on a train, and keeping sand or sunscreen off the bezel. When the forecast is heavy rain or you are heading somewhere damp:

  • Rain and splash: the Kindle itself is the waterproof part. Prefer a folio or fabric cover that closes fully so the screen stays dry and clean; Amazon rates its 2026 Page-Turn Cover IPX8 as well, but that accessory is Signature-only.
  • Beach, pool, boat: sand and salt are harder on ports and hinges than rain. A clear waterproof pouch that holds the whole Kindle (case on or off) is the usual extra layer; it is not a substitute for buying the right model-year fit.
  • Bags and flights: a sleeve or a closed folio beats a bare shell in a stuffed tote. If you pre-ordered the 2026 Paperwhite (US ship date October 28, 2026), wait for a listing that names 2026 before packing a new case for the trip.

We are not tying this advice to any particular storm or region; treat it as evergreen travel hygiene for a waterproof e-reader. Style trade-offs stay in the table above.

Signature Edition and charging

The Signature Edition changes which case is safe in a few specific ways, so check these before buying.

  • 2021 and 2024: the Signature Edition has Qi wireless charging, and standard models do not. If you use a Qi pad, look for a non-metal cover and a listing that says it works with wireless charging, then test with the case on. A cover that blocks the charge will usually not tell you so on the box.
  • 2026: Launch coverage reports pogo pins for a dock sold separately and no Qi wireless charging on the Signature Edition. A case should leave the pins clear if you plan to use that dock or the Page-Turn Cover.
  • Docks and stands: Amazon's docks are model-specific; see our Kindle stand guide.
  • All models: cable charging is the baseline: USB-C on 2021 and later models, micro-USB on 2018 and older (see our Kindle charger guide). A cover with a tight, well-placed cutout is better than one that makes you remove the case every time.

Weight is the other point. The Signature Edition is a few grams heavier than the standard model in 2021 and 2024; for 2026, secondary sources put Signature at 229 g versus 204 g. For the full comparison of the editions, see the Signature section of our Paperwhite guide.

Do you need a screen protector?

Mostly not, and it depends on which case you choose. A folio that closes over the screen already does the job, so a protector adds little. A slim shell, which leaves the front exposed, or a Kindle that rides loose in a bag is where one might make sense. Amazon described the 2018 Paperwhite's screen as plastic and highly shatter-resistant and scratch-resistant, according to CNET's launch preview. We have not verified the equivalent claim for later models, so do not assume a protector is unnecessary or required.

If you buy one, buy a screen protector made for your model year and size, because a 6.8-inch protector will not cover a 7-inch screen. Read reviews for glare, bubbles and touch response, since a matte or glossy film can change the look of the glare-free display that people buy a Paperwhite for. We have not tested any, so we are not recommending one. For the 2026 model, the same "wait for a listing that names it" rule applies as for cases.

Listing red flags

  • No generation or release year in the title. "Fits Kindle Paperwhite" is not specific enough.
  • "Fits 6.8-inch and 7-inch" or any listing that spans several generations. No hard case is cut for that range.
  • Titles that stack many generations (for example "13th/12th/11th Gen" or "2026/2024/2021" plus Colorsoft in one line). After the 2026 announcement, some third-party listings already claim multi-year fit before US buyers have the new device. That is a signal to slow down, not a reason to buy; we do not recommend or rank those brands.
  • A 2024 case marketed for the 2026 model without reviews from real buyers who own the 2026 device (US ship date October 28, 2026).
  • Reviews complaining of fit. Sort by recent and search for "too tight," "button" and "port."
  • Stock images of the wrong device, such as a power button in the wrong place for your model.
  • Language suggesting official approval. A third-party case is a third-party case, and a seller calling itself "official" or "Amazon certified" deserves extra suspicion. We do not use such language on this site either.
  • A return window you cannot see. Fit is the main reason cases go back; buy where returns are easy.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best case for a Kindle Paperwhite?

There is no single best Kindle Paperwhite case, because "Paperwhite" covers several different bodies. The best case is the one whose listing names your exact model year and generation, closes magnetically with auto sleep/wake, and has clean cutouts for the power button and USB-C. After that it is a style choice: a folio for everyday carry, a slim shell if you dislike bulk, a strap case for one-handed reading. See the style table.

Will a 2024 Paperwhite case fit the 2026 Paperwhite?

No. Treat them as different bodies. The 2026 model is about 0.8 mm narrower and 2 mm shorter than the 2024 model (126.8 × 174.7 × 6.8 mm versus 127.6 × 176.7 × 7.8 mm), the power button moved from the bottom edge to the right edge, and Amazon's own 2024 fabric cover is listed for the 2024 release only. Amazon's 2026 knit cover is listed for 2026 Paperwhite and Colorsoft releases only. See the 2026 section.

Does a 2021 Paperwhite case fit the 2024 model?

Not reliably. The 2021 model is 6.8-inch and about 124.6 mm wide; the 2024 model is 7-inch and 127.6 mm wide and slightly taller. Amazon's fabric cover for the 2021 models is listed as 11th generation only and "will not fit prior generation" devices, and the 2024 cover is listed for the 2024 release only. A hard shell is the least forgiving, and a few millimeters decide whether it snaps on.

Do I need a different Kindle Paperwhite case for the Signature Edition?

For 2021 and 2024, the Signature Edition shares its body with the standard Paperwhite, so cases are usually listed for both, but read the listing. For 2026, the Signature Edition has an aluminum back and pogo pins for the dock and the Page-Turn Cover; secondary sources put its weight at 229 g versus 204 g for the standard model, with the same footprint. A case that is not explicitly listed for the Signature Edition could block those pins. Amazon says the $79.99 Page-Turn Cover works with the Signature Edition only.

Can I wirelessly charge my Paperwhite with a case on?

Only the 2021 and 2024 Signature Editions support Qi wireless charging; standard models do not, and the 2026 Signature Edition uses pogo pins for a dock sold separately instead. If you do use Qi, thin non-metal covers are the safest bet, and a listing that says it works with wireless charging beats guesswork. For USB-C charging, look for a case with a port cutout, or one that Amazon says can stay on while charging.

Is a Kindle Paperwhite case worth it if the device is waterproof?

Waterproofing and protection are different jobs. IPX8 (2 meters of fresh water for 60 minutes) covers immersion on the 2018, 2021, 2024 and — per Amazon's UK product page — 2026 Paperwhite models. That rating is not about scratches from keys in a bag or a drop onto a hard floor. A cover is optional if the Kindle stays at home and needed more if it travels.

Will a 2026 Paperwhite case fit Kindle Colorsoft?

Amazon's 2026 knit fabric cover listing names both Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft (2026 releases only). That does not mean every third-party Paperwhite case will fit Colorsoft. For Colorsoft-specific notes, see our Kindle Colorsoft case guide.

Do I need a waterproof case if my Paperwhite is already IPX8?

Usually no dedicated waterproof case. Amazon rates recent Paperwhites (including 2026 per the UK product page) IPX8 for fresh-water immersion. That covers rain and splash on the device itself; it does not cover sand, sunscreen, salt spray, or knocks in a bag. For wet or messy trips, a closed folio or a clear dry pouch over the whole device is the extra layer — see the waterproof-pouch row in case styles and travel and wet weather. A case is still useful for scratches and drops even when the Kindle itself is waterproof.

Should I use a screen protector or a case?

If you buy a folio that closes over the screen, a protector is mostly redundant. A shell or a bare Kindle in a bag is where a protector might help. See our screen protector note: buy only one listed for your model year, and be wary of anything that adds glare or hurts touch response.

Who can use the Amazon Page-Turn Cover?

Amazon's Page-Turn Cover (ASIN B0H4WGJMPD, $79.99) is listed for Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition and Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition, 2026 releases only. It attaches magnetically over the Signature pogo pins, has physical page-turn buttons, needs no battery or pairing, and Amazon's listing rates the cover IPX8. The standard (non-Signature) 2026 Paperwhite cannot use it. If you want page-turn buttons without that cover, Amazon's $34.99 Kindle Click Bluetooth remote is a separate option — see our page turner guide.

Can I trust a third-party case that says it fits every Paperwhite generation?

Be skeptical. Hard cases are cut for one body. Listings that stack "13th/12th/11th Generation" or "2026/2024/2021" and Colorsoft in the same title are a red flag, especially before US buyers have received the 2026 device (ships October 28, 2026). Prefer a title that names your exact model year, then read the most recent reviews for fit and button cutouts. We do not rank or endorse third-party brands.

Are Amazon's own covers better than third-party cases?

They are easier to buy correctly, because they are made for a named model and sold with it in the title. They usually cost more. Third-party cases are plentiful for the 2021 and 2024 models, where fit and cutout problems show up in reviews you can read. For the 2026 Paperwhite before many third-party reviews exist, Amazon's covers are the less risky place to start.

How do I find out which Paperwhite I have?

Look at the screen size and the power button. A 6-inch Paperwhite with a flush front is the 2018 (10th gen) model; 6.8-inch is 2021 (11th gen); 7-inch with a bottom power button is 2024 (12th gen); a 7-inch with the power button on the right edge is the 2026 model. For certainty, check the device information in Settings and the device list in your Amazon account, then compare against the listing's generation and release year.

A Kindle Scribe is the one Kindle where the case has a second job: keeping the pen with the device. It is also the one where model year matters most, because Amazon has now sold three Scribe models in about four years, and the newest is a different size from the older two. A case for the 10.2-inch Scribe will not fit the 11-inch Scribe, and a case that holds the screen well may still let the pen fall off in a bag. This page sorts the choices by model year, explains how the pen is stored on each, and shows which kinds of case suit how you write.

  • 2025 Kindle Scribe or Scribe Colorsoft (11-inch): buy a case that names the 2025 release (the third-generation Scribe) and, for the Colorsoft, a listing that names it too. Amazon's own folios start at $89.99; third-party folios with pen holders cost less.

  • All of them: pick the pen storage you will actually use (loop, holder, clasp, or flap), check the cutouts and the auto sleep/wake, and try the folded-stand position quickly for pen interference.
  • Do not mix up the Paperwhite and the Scribe. The Paperwhite is 7-inch; see our Paperwhite case guide. For styles and materials that apply to every Kindle, see the Kindle case buying guide.

Step 1: Identify your Scribe

"Kindle Scribe" covers three models now across two body sizes, and the generation numbers on listings are confusing. Start from what you can see:

  • 10.2-inch screen, wide grip bezel along one side, narrow bezel on the other: the 2022 or 2024 model. The Verge describes the redesign as doing "away with the asymmetrical chin on one side," which is what the old models had. If the bezel around the screen is white, it is the 2024 model; the 2022 model shipped only in Tungsten, a gray-metal color.
  • 11-inch screen with even, narrow bezels and a power button at the upper right: the 2025 Kindle Scribe or Kindle Scribe Colorsoft. IGN and TechRadar both place the power button on the upper right side, the USB-C port at the bottom, and the pen on the right side just under the button.

Then check the generation text in your device settings and your Amazon account's device list. Be careful with the numbers: Amazon's UK listing for the 2024 model reads "Kindle Scribe 1st generation - 2024 release," and a reader on a Kindle blog reports the device itself shows "1st generation, 2024 Release," whereas Amazon's 2025 listings read "3rd Generation" for the black-and-white model and "1st Gen" for the Colorsoft. The release year is the safer matching key. A listing that says only "fits Kindle Scribe" is not specific enough.

The 2025 Scribe and Colorsoft are therefore the latest we could verify. Check Amazon's product page for anything announced after October 2, 2026.

2025 Scribe and Scribe Colorsoft cases

Amazon announced the redesigned Scribe lineup on September 30, 2025: the Kindle Scribe, a Kindle Scribe without a front light, and the first color Scribe, the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft, all 11-inch, 5.4 mm thick and 400 g by Amazon's figures. At announcement, The Verge listed prices of $499.99 for the standard Scribe, $629.99 for the Colorsoft and $429.99 for the no-front-light model, which was due early in 2026. Amazon's Australian page for the same lineup is dated May 14, 2026, so launch timing differs by country.

What a case buyer needs to know:

  • New body: 189 × 245 mm, 5.4 mm thick (Amazon's and TechRadar's figures for the Colorsoft; Amazon's listing for the no-front-light model gives the same numbers). It has no wide grip bezel, so it is closer to a tablet shape than the old Scribes.
  • Pen on the right side: the pen attaches magnetically just below the power button, per IGN. TechRadar calls this placement "a silly design choice" given the pen is short enough to sit on top, and Trusted Reviews says the magnet is not the strongest.
  • Amazon's covers: a plant-based leather folio ($89.99 on its listing today) with a pen holder, a magnetic-attach body, a stand with low and high angles and auto wake; and the Executive Folio ($139.99), a notebook-style folio in pebbled leather with a magnetic flap that secures the pen or tucks away. Both are described as "compatible only with 2025 Kindle Scribe releases."
  • Third-party: MoKo, Fintie and CoBak all list 2025 Scribe cases that also name the Colorsoft, with pen holders, clasps or flaps, and auto sleep/wake. We saw a MoKo listing at $47.49 with 4.4 stars from 287 reviews. We have not tested any of them.

What we could not confirm

We could not confirm a separate case size for the Colorsoft: the spec listings we found match the 2025 black-and-white Scribe, but independent reviewers report slightly different weights (Trusted Reviews gives 393 g against Amazon's 400 g), and we have not measured either device. We also could not verify how a screen protector affects writing on the new textured glass. If you buy a case listed for the Colorsoft, check that the listing names your exact device. The 7-inch Kindle Colorsoft is a different device with its own cases; see our Kindle Colorsoft case guide.

Search Amazon: 11-inch Scribe cases

2024 Scribe cases

Amazon announced the reimagined Kindle Scribe on October 16, 2024, with shipping from December 4 and pre-orders from $399.99. It is 10.2 inches with white screen borders, 196 × 230 × 5.7 mm and 433 g, and it comes only with the Premium Pen, whose eraser is soft and whose body is aluminum, per Digital Trends. The pen is 162 × 8.8 × 8.4 mm by Amazon's UK listing, and it attaches magnetically to the side. Amazon's FAQ says the pen never needs to be charged.

For cases, the choices are wide because the body is shared with the 2022 model. Amazon's own plant-based leather folio (with a microfiber interior) lists a $79.99 price today, with a pen holder, stand angles and auto wake; the listing says it is compatible with 2024 and 2022. Third-party "2024/2022" cases are common, with hard back shells, PU leather, built-in pen holders and card slots.

Two cautions. First, the secure fit of Amazon's folio: On Amazon's listing, 32 of the 53 reviews that mention secure fit are negative, with some saying the magnets let the Scribe come loose. Second, since the 2025 models look like the same product family, relabelled listings that add 2025 to a 2024 case are worth treating with suspicion; read the title and the recent reviews and make sure the dimensions in the listing say 10.2-inch for the 2024 model.

Search Amazon: 10.2-inch Scribe cases

2022 Scribe cases

The first Kindle Scribe was announced on September 28, 2022 and shipped on November 30, 2022 from $339. It has the same 10.2-inch 300 ppi display, 433 g weight and 5.8 mm thickness per Amazon's press release and Ebook Friendly's spec table. It shipped with a choice of Basic Pen or Premium Pen, both battery-free and magnetically attached on the side. The Basic Pen has no eraser or shortcut button.

Amazon launched fabric, leather and premium leather covers with it, which fold to prop the Scribe up at an angle; Ebook Friendly describes a stylus loop on the front cover. Ebook Friendly also notes that the port and power button are on the wide grip side of the old design and the pen magnet on the opposite one, so third-party cases need a long cutout or an open edge for the pen. Those original covers are older stock now. Today the plant-based folio that lists both years is the one that is easy to find. If you have a 2022 Scribe and a working case, there is no need to buy another for the new software, since The eBook Reader reports that Amazon pushed the new note-taking and AI features to the 2022 model by software update on the 2024 model's launch day.

The pen: how it attaches and how cases hold it

Every Scribe pen is battery-free and clings to the side by a magnet. A Kindle Scribe has no pen slot or garage, so storage is a case feature. These are the common approaches.

Magnets, stands and the pen

Looking for a separate stand for the Scribe? See our Kindle stand guide; for how folio and magnetic-attach covers differ, see Kindle covers explained.

The Scribe senses the pen through the screen, and some owners report that magnets in a cover can disturb it. Several Amazon reviewers of the 2025 plant-based folio say the magnets interfered with the pen when the cover was folded behind the device as a stand, with problems about 60% of the way down the page in one account, while others of the same cover found the magnets strong and trouble free. Forum threads of the same kind exist for the older models. We have not tested this, so treat it as a risk to check, not a fact about any product.

  • Test the case in the position you will actually write in, for example folded behind with the stand angle, within the first days of owning it.
  • If the pen lines drift or skip in one area, remove the case and test again. If the issue goes away, the case is the cause and it is time for a return.
  • A case with a non-magnetic closure (elastic, snap) avoids the problem, but its pen storage may differ.
  • Buy where a return is easy; this is not something a listing page can promise.

Materials

The same trade-offs apply as on other Kindles, with a few Scribe twists. Amazon's plant-based leather is made from more than 70% renewable bio-materials, with the rest polyurethane, according to the 2025 folio listing. Its Executive Folio is described as full-grain pebbled leather from suppliers rated Gold by the Leather Working Group, although some reviewers on that listing say it feels like PU, so the material label alone is a poor guide. The PU leather in many third-party cases is common and cheaper; hard shells add protection and weight.

Weight matters here more than on a small Kindle. The 2025 Scribe is 400 g and the 2024 model 433 g, and MoKo's 2025 listing states 400 g, which would double the weight if it refers to the case (we could not confirm what the figure covers). Check what the cover adds before you decide, and look for "microfiber lining" or similar if you want something soft against the glass. Our materials section on the general guide has the basic comparison.

Listing red flags

  • "Fits Kindle Scribe" with no year. There are two body sizes (10.2-inch and 11-inch) and three model years; one case does not fit all.
  • "10.2-inch and 11-inch" or a listing that spans both families. No fitted case is cut for both.
  • A 2024 case that suddenly claims to fit the 2025 models, without reviews from 2025 owners.
  • No pen storage shown for the model year you own. A pen loop sized for another pen length can be loose.
  • Reviews complaining that the Scribe falls out or that the pen skips. Sort by recent and search "magnet," "falls," "pen."
  • Language suggesting official approval. A third-party case is a third-party case; we do not use "official" or "Amazon certified" for anything here.
  • A return window you cannot see. Fit and magnet behavior are hard to judge from photos.

How we researched this

This guide uses Amazon's announcements, product pages and listings, and coverage from The Verge, TechRadar, IGN, Trusted Reviews, PCMag, Digital Trends and Ebook Friendly. We do not review products in a lab and we have not tested individual cases or handled any Scribe. We do not rank third-party cases or claim any is endorsed by Amazon; the third-party brands named above are ones we saw in listings, not recommendations. Prices change and are a snapshot from October 2, 2026. Where sources disagree (such as the 2024 model's water rating, or small weight differences) we say so. To report a mistake, use our contact page; our approach is described in our editorial policy.

  • Amazon press releases: "Introducing Amazon Kindle Scribe" (Sept 28, 2022) and "Amazon Launches Entirely New Kindle Lineup" (Oct 16, 2024): launch dates, prices, pen description.
  • Amazon, "Kindle Scribe FAQ" and "Amazon unveils redesigned Kindle Scribe lineup" (aboutamazon.com): pen, waterproofing, 2025 lineup details.
  • Amazon.com listings: Kindle Scribe without Front Light (2025), the plant-based and Executive folios for 2022/2024 and 2025, and Amazon UK's 2024 Scribe listing: dimensions, compatibility wording, prices checked October 2, 2026.
  • The Verge, Sept 30, 2025 announcement; TechRadar, IGN and Trusted Reviews on the Scribe Colorsoft: size, button and pen placement, weak magnet.
  • PCMag and Digital Trends reviews of the 2024 Scribe; Ebook Friendly's 2022 spec table; The eBook Reader's 2022-vs-2024 comparison: size, pen interchangeability.
  • Amazon's "new Kindle lineup" announcement (aboutamazon.com, Oct 1, 2026): used to confirm no newer Scribe was announced with it.

Frequently asked questions

Does a 2022 Kindle Scribe case fit the 2024 Scribe?

Usually yes, if the listing names both. Amazon lists its plant-based leather folio as "compatible only with Kindle Scribe 2024 and 2022 releases," and PCMag's 2024 review says the two Scribes are close enough in size to fit Amazon's accessory case interchangeably. Many third-party listings are titled "2024/2022" as well. The 2024 model is the same 10.2-inch panel in a body that is only fractions of a millimeter different, so the risk is low, but still read the listing.

Will a 2024 Scribe case fit the 2025 Kindle Scribe or Scribe Colorsoft?

No. The 2025 models have an 11-inch screen and a different body (189 × 245 × 5.4 mm against 196 × 230 × 5.7 mm for 2024), and Amazon's 2025 folio listings say "compatible only with 2025 Kindle Scribe releases." The 2024 cover is listed for 2024 and 2022 only. The two bodies are shaped differently as well, because the 2025 models dropped the wide grip bezel, so there is no pushing a 2024 case onto a 2025 device.

Is the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft the same size as the 2025 Kindle Scribe?

Amazon's announcement gives the same 5.4 mm thickness and 400 g for the redesigned lineup, and the Colorsoft spec listings we found give the same 189 × 245 × 5.4 mm body as the black-and-white 2025 Scribe. Third-party cases from MoKo and Fintie are listed for both in one title. We did not measure either device, and independent reviews report slightly different weights, so a case listed for both is a sensible filter, not a guarantee.

Where does the pen go, and does the Scribe have a pen slot?

There is no built-in pen garage on any Scribe. The Premium Pen clings to the side of the device with a magnet (Amazon: "attaches magnetically"). On the 2025 models it sits on the right side, just below the power button. Trusted Reviews says the magnet is not the strongest and the pen will likely fall off in a bag, and TechRadar dislikes the placement. That is why most folios add a pen loop, holder, clasp or flap. See the pen section.

Do magnets in a Scribe folio affect the pen?

They can, in some positions. The Scribe's pen uses a pen-sensing layer, and several Amazon reviewers of the 2025 plant-based folio say its magnets interfered with the pen when the cover was folded behind into a stand, with errors partway down the page. Others report no problem. This is anecdotal, not a test, but it is the reason to check the return window and to try the case in your usual writing position straight away.

Is the Kindle Scribe waterproof, and does it need a case?

Amazon's own Scribe FAQ says no: the Scribe is not waterproof and Amazon does not recommend using it in a tub or pool. One review's spec table lists an IPX8 rating for the 2024 model, which contradicts Amazon, so we follow Amazon. A cover will not make it waterproof. What a case does is protect a thin, expensive screen from scratches and knocks, and Trusted Reviews, who used the Colorsoft without one, still recommend one given the price.

Which Scribe do I have?

If one side has a wide, textured grip bezel and the other side is narrow, you have the 2022 or 2024 model (10.2-inch). The 2024 model has white bezels around the screen. If the bezels are even and narrow all round and the screen is 11 inches, it is a 2025 Scribe or Scribe Colorsoft. A note on labels: the device information screen for the 2024 model has been reported to read "1st generation, 2024 release," and Amazon's UK listing uses the same wording, while the 2025 listings say "3rd Generation," so use release year, not generation number, when matching a case.

Are Amazon's Scribe folios worth the price compared with third-party cases?

That is a value judgment, and Amazon's own reviewers are split. On the listings we checked, the 2025 plant-based folio is $89.99 and the Executive Folio is $139.99; the 2022/2024 plant-based folio showed $79.99. Reviewers on those pages call them nicely made but overpriced, and a large share of the reviews on the 2022/2024 folio say the magnets do not hold the device securely enough. Third-party folios with a snap-in or hard back are cheaper (for example, a MoKo 2025 listing at $47.49) but vary in fit. Buy where returns are easy.

Do I need a screen protector on a Scribe?

We have no tested recommendation. Amazon says the 2025 Scribe has texture-molded glass to give the pen friction, so a film could change the writing feel, and we have not verified how any film behaves. A folio that closes over the screen already guards it in a bag. If you add a protector anyway, buy one made for your exact size, because a 10.2-inch film will not cover an 11-inch panel.

Kindle Paperwhite Cover: Fit, Types and How to Choose

Facts checked October 19, 2026. Independent guide based on Amazon's announcements, product pages and launch coverage. We have not hands-on tested any cover mentioned, and we have not handled the 2026 Paperwhite.

Affiliate disclosure: Links to Amazon on this page are ordinary Amazon.com links. We are not Amazon and are not an authorized Amazon reseller. We may join the Amazon Associates program; if we do, qualifying links will carry a tracking tag and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you, and our disclosure page will say so. Our picks and wording are not paid for. Prices and specs change; the Amazon listing is the source of truth.

Searching for a "Kindle Paperwhite cover" usually means two decisions at once: whether a folio flap, a back shell or a sleeve is the right construction, and whether the listing matches your exact Paperwhite year. This page answers both. It starts with what to check before you buy a Paperwhite cover, then compares cover types, and links out to model-year fit tables when you are ready to shop.

The short answer: what to check for a Paperwhite cover

  • Match the model year in the title. A 2024 cover does not fit the 2026 Paperwhite (different footprint and power-button position). Amazon's 2026 knit cover is $44.99 and lists 2026 Paperwhite + Colorsoft only; the lineup announcement still says covers from $39.99.
  • Decide flap vs no flap. A folio covers the screen in a bag and usually adds auto wake/sleep; a back shell adds grip without a flap; a sleeve protects only in transit.
  • Check cutouts and magnets. Power button (bottom edge on 2024, right edge on 2026), USB-C, and auto wake/sleep alignment. Signature buyers: do not block pogo pins if you want Amazon's dock or Page-Turn Cover.
  • Need year-by-year case tables? Use the Paperwhite case guide. Choosing the device itself? See which Paperwhite to buy. Everything else: accessories hub.

  • "I do not know whether I want a flap, a shell or a sleeve": read the type comparison below.
  • "I just want to carry my Kindle in a bag": a Kindle sleeve may be all you need.
  • "I want to prop my Kindle up": see the Kindle stand guide; a folio that folds into a stand is covered here under features.

Cover vs case: what the words mean

There is no official line between the two words, so it helps to be clear about how this site uses them. Amazon's own accessory announcement for the 2026 lineup uses "Kindle Covers" for what are, in effect, folios: knit fabric, plant-based leather and pebbled premium leather versions that "wrap fully around the device." Retailers and third-party sellers mostly say "case" for the same kind of product, plus shells, bumpers and sleeves. We cannot see what any individual shopper means when typing either word, so we treat them as overlapping and split by construction instead.

A four-step way to choose

Instead of starting from a list of products, narrow in layers, from the choice that matters most to the one that matters least:

  1. Coverage: flap over the screen or not. This decides how the Kindle behaves in a bag.
  2. Material: fabric, synthetic leather, plant-based leather or premium leather. This decides feel, weight and how it ages.
  3. Features: auto wake/sleep, a stand mode, a strap, a pen holder (Scribe), and charging or accessory compatibility.
  4. Model fit: the exact model year in the listing title. This is the step most likely to cause a return, and it lives on the model guides.

Step 1: Full-wrap folio vs back cover

The biggest decision is whether anything closes over the screen. A folio protects it; a back cover protects everything else and gets out of the way.
