One note on drops: no cover can promise protection, and we have no drop tests. The practical difference is that a snap-in or wrap-around design holds the Kindle through its own frame, while a magnetic-attach design relies on magnets alone. Amazon's own wording on its Scribe folio listing is that the device "magnetically attaches to a slim folio, rather than snapping into a plastic back like a traditional Kindle cover." That is a deliberate trade for thinness, and it is why some reviewers on that listing say the grip is not secure enough.

Step 2: Fabric, synthetic, plant-based or leather

The second layer is how it feels in the hand. These are general trade-offs, not rankings.

MaterialWhat to expectWatch out for

If you are on the fence, ask what you will actually notice. A cover that is a few grams lighter matters every day if you hold a Kindle in one hand in bed, whereas the difference between synthetic and plant-based leather matters mostly in how it looks after a year. We cannot tell you which one lasts longer, because we have not tested any.

Step 3: Auto wake/sleep and other features

  • Auto wake/sleep. A magnet in the flap tells the Kindle to wake when opened and sleep when closed; Amazon describes its covers as doing exactly that. It is a convenience: the Kindle also sleeps on its own after a timeout. It only works when the magnet lines up with the device, which is another reason to match the model year exactly.
  • Stand mode. Many folios fold back to prop the Kindle at one or two angles. Amazon's 2025 Scribe folio listing, for example, mentions low and high stand angles. A cover stand is convenient for a tray table; for a desk or bed, a dedicated stand may be steadier.
  • Hand strap. Helps in bed and on a train. It adds a little bulk.
  • Pen holder (Scribe only). The Scribe's pen clings to the side by a magnet and has no slot, so folios add a loop, clasp or flap. Details are in the Scribe case guide.
  • Charging and accessories. The 2022 and 2024 Signature Edition wireless dock charges with a case up to 4 mm thick; the 2026 Signature Editions use pogo pins at the back for a dock and for Amazon's Page-Turn Cover. A cover that blocks them blocks those accessories. Our Kindle charger guide covers charging with a case on.
  • Page-turn buttons. Amazon's $79.99 Page-Turn Cover adds physical buttons for the 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition and Colorsoft Signature Edition. The $34.99 Kindle Click is a separate Bluetooth remote that Amazon says works with all new Kindles and any Kindle from 2024 or later, so it needs no special cover. See our Kindle page turner guide for a comparison.

Magnetic-attach vs snap-in

This is the cover-specific question that most buyers do not realize they are answering. In the 2026 lineup Amazon sells two constructions. For the plastic models, its covers "wrap fully around the device," per Amazon's announcement. For the aluminum models, it sells "slim magnetic-attach covers." The Verge notes the aluminum 6-inch Kindle can magnetically attach to a folio case priced at $49.99.

The practical effect is on how the Kindle comes out of the cover. A snap-in or wrap design takes some effort to remove; a magnetic-attach design lifts off. That is convenient for taking the Kindle out and potentially a risk if the magnets are weak or the Kindle is dropped. For the Scribe, a magnetic folio also puts a second magnet near the pen's writing area, and reviewers on one 2025 folio listing report pen interference when the cover is folded back (anecdotal, not tested). If you write on your Kindle, read the Scribe magnets section.

Amazon's own covers

As of October 19, 2026, here is what we could verify from Amazon and press coverage:

  • 2026 lineup: Amazon's announcement (Oct 1, 2026) lists Kindle Covers starting at $39.99 in knit fabric, plant-based leather and pebbled premium leather, color-matched across the lineup, plus slim magnetic-attach covers for aluminum devices, a $79.99 Page-Turn Cover and a $59.99 charging dock for the Signature Editions. The knit fabric cover listing we checked (ASIN B0H6H9MM86) is $44.99 and states it fits Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft 2026 releases only.
  • 2024 Paperwhite: retailers list Amazon's fabric cover as fitting the 2024 release only.
  • Scribe: the plant-based folio for the 2022 and 2024 Scribe listed at $79.99 and the 2025 version at $89.99; the Executive Folio at $139.99 (Amazon.com listings checked earlier in October 2026; see the Scribe guide for caveats).

Third-party covers are cheaper and far more varied. Because the words overlap, the same listings appear whether you search "Kindle cover" or "Kindle case." We name no third-party winners; see our Amazon vs third-party section for how we think about it. The 2026 Paperwhite ships October 28, 2026, so listings for it are still early.

Search Amazon: Kindle Paperwhite covers

Cover type by how you read

Our reasoning, not test results.
If you…Start withWhy
Toss your Kindle in a bag dailyFolio with auto wake/sleepThe flap protects the screen and the Kindle sleeps when you shut it.
Read one-handed in bedBack cover or slim folio, maybe a strapLess to fold back; less weight on the wrist.
Mostly read at homePossibly nothing, or a back cover for gripThe Kindle is thin and the Paperwhite is waterproof.
Read near waterFabric cover that dries quickly, or noneAmazon describes its 2024 fabric cover as water-safe; a wet leatherette cover can take longer to dry.
Write on a ScribeA folio with a pen loop, clasp or flapSee the Scribe case guide.
Care most about thinnessSlim magnetic-attach folioTrade-off: the device relies on magnets for grip.

Step 4: Match the model

Once you know the type, the last step is the one that decides whether it works. Here is where to go:

Where to check fit for each Kindle family.
Your KindleGo to
Paperwhite (2026, 2024, 2021, 2018 and older)Kindle Paperwhite case guide
Kindle Colorsoft (2024, 2025, 2026)Kindle Colorsoft case guide
Scribe and Scribe Colorsoft (2022, 2024, 2025)Kindle Scribe case guide
Basic Kindle, Oasis, or not sureFit section of the Kindle case buying guide
Choosing the device itselfKindle Paperwhite: which one to buy

Cover-specific red flags

  • "Fits all Kindle Paperwhite." The generations differ in size and, on the 2026 model, button position. See the case guides.
  • A listing that spans a 2024 and a 2026 device without reviews from 2026 owners, since the 2026 Paperwhite was still a pre-order when we checked.
  • No mention of auto wake/sleep on a folio you expect it from.
  • Pogo-pin area covered on a Signature Edition when you plan to use Amazon's dock or Page-Turn Cover.
  • Reviews saying the Kindle falls out of a magnetic-attach folio. Sort by recent and search "falls," "loose," "magnet."
  • "Official" or "Amazon certified" wording on a non-Amazon product. We do not use that language on this site either.

How we researched this

This guide uses Amazon's October 1, 2026 lineup announcement, Amazon.com listings, retailer listings for Amazon's 2024 fabric cover, Amazon UK's 2026 Paperwhite product page, and coverage from The Verge, WIRED and Engadget. We refreshed Paperwhite cover fit notes on October 19, 2026. We have not tested any cover and do not rank third-party products. Price figures are snapshots from October 19, 2026. Where terms overlap or sources conflict, we say so. To report a mistake, use our contact page; our approach is described in the editorial policy.

  • Amazon, "The new Amazon Kindle lineup" (aboutamazon.com), Oct 1, 2026: covers from $39.99, Page-Turn Cover, dock, Kindle Click.
  • Amazon.com knit fabric cover listing (ASIN B0H6H9MM86), checked October 19, 2026: $44.99, 2026 Paperwhite and Colorsoft only.
  • Amazon.co.uk Kindle Paperwhite product page, checked October 19, 2026: IPX8 (2 m fresh water, 60 minutes).
  • Xataka, Case Society Co, Read with Pro (Oct 2026): 2026 Paperwhite 126.8 × 174.7 × 6.8 mm and Signature weight ~229 g, citing Amazon product data (secondary sources; not pulled from an Amazon US tech card by us).
  • The Verge and WIRED, Oct 1, 2026: aluminum Kindle folio price, power button move, device weights.
  • Amazon.com listings for the plant-based and Executive Scribe folios and the Wireless Charging Dock (4 mm case limit), checked in October 2026.
  • Retailer listings of Amazon's 2024 Paperwhite fabric cover (Best Buy Canada, JB Hi-Fi): fit and material notes.

Frequently asked questions

Will a 2024 Kindle Paperwhite cover fit the 2026 Paperwhite?

No. Treat them as different bodies. The 2026 Paperwhite is about 0.8 mm narrower and 2 mm shorter than the 2024 model (126.8 × 174.7 × 6.8 mm versus 127.6 × 176.7 × 7.8 mm, secondary sources citing Amazon product data), the power button moved from the bottom edge to the right edge, and Amazon's own 2024 fabric cover is listed for the 2024 release only. Amazon's 2026 knit cover (ASIN B0H6H9MM86, $44.99) is listed for 2026 Paperwhite and Colorsoft releases only. See 2026 vs 2024 Paperwhite cover fit.

Is a Kindle cover the same thing as a Kindle case?

Not formally. There is no industry standard, and sellers use both words for the same products. Amazon calls its own folios "Kindle Covers," while most third-party listings say "case." On this site, "cover" means a folio-style product with a front flap that closes over the screen, and "case" is the wider family that also includes back shells, bumpers and sleeves. If you are choosing by model year for a Paperwhite, start with the Kindle Paperwhite case guide; if you are choosing between a flap and no flap, this page is the right one. The general Kindle case buying guide covers fit red flags for every Kindle.

Will a 2026 Paperwhite cover fit Kindle Colorsoft?

Amazon's 2026 knit fabric cover listing names both Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft (2026 releases only). That does not mean every third-party Paperwhite cover will fit Colorsoft. For Colorsoft-specific notes, see our Kindle Colorsoft case guide.

Do I need a cover if my Kindle is waterproof?

Water rating and scratch protection are different things. Amazon's 2018, 2021 and 2024 Paperwhite models are rated IPX8 (2 meters of fresh water for 60 minutes), and Amazon's UK product page rates the 2026 Paperwhite the same way. A cover does not add to that. What a front flap adds is protection for the screen against keys, pens and corners in a bag. If your Kindle lives at home, you may want nothing, or just a back shell for grip.

What is auto wake/sleep, and does every cover have it?

Auto wake/sleep means the Kindle wakes when you open the cover and goes to sleep when you close it. Amazon describes its own covers as doing this, and most folio-style third-party listings advertise it too. Back shells and sleeves generally do not have it, because they have no flap to trigger it. It is a convenience, not a necessity: the Kindle sleeps by itself after a timeout. Check that "auto wake/sleep" appears in the listing for your exact model, and do not assume a cover made for another model year has the magnet in the right place.

Is a full-wrap folio better than a back cover?

It depends on the risk you are trying to avoid. A folio protects the screen when closed and keeps dust and pocket debris off it. A back cover (a shell) leaves the screen open, so it adds grip and edge protection without a flap in your way, but it does nothing for a screen in a bag. Neither is better in general. If your Kindle travels in a bag with other things, a folio makes more sense; if it mostly sits on a nightstand and you want something to hold on to, a shell might.

Can I charge my Kindle on a dock or wirelessly with a cover on?

Sometimes, and the limit is in the dock's specification. Amazon's wireless charging dock for the 2022 and 2024 Signature Editions and the Colorsoft Signature Edition says it charges with a case up to 4 mm thick, in portrait mode, and its reviews show mixed experiences when a case is on. The 2026 Signature Editions use pogo pins on the back for Amazon's $59.99 dock and $79.99 Page-Turn Cover, so a cover that blocks those pins also blocks those accessories. See our Kindle stand guide for more on docks.

Is plant-based leather the same as leather?

No. Amazon describes its plant-based leather folio for the Scribe as made from more than 70% renewable bio-materials, with the remainder polyurethane, so it is a synthetic-leaning material. Amazon separately sells "premium leather" or pebbled leather covers described as leather (its Scribe Executive Folio is described as full-grain pebbled leather). Third-party "PU leather" is a polyurethane coating. Reviewers on some listings say premium-priced covers feel like PU, so the label alone is a poor guide. Read the material line, and the recent reviews that mention it.

Will a cover make my Kindle much heavier?

It adds weight, and how much varies by product, which is why we avoid giving a single number. Amazon's weights for the bare devices are a useful baseline: about 158 g for the 2022 and 2024 Kindle, 211 g for the 2024 Paperwhite, 219 g for the Colorsoft Signature Edition, and WIRED reports 204 g for the 2026 Paperwhite (Signature about 229 g from secondary sources). Some Amazon reviewers say an official cover makes a Paperwhite feel noticeably heavier. If weight matters, look for the cover's own weight in the listing, or choose a back cover or a slim magnetic-attach folio.

Kindle Sleeve: How to Choose the Right Size and Material

Facts checked October 19, 2026. Independent guide based on Amazon's specifications and listings. We have not hands-on tested any sleeve or measured any Kindle, including the 2026 Paperwhite.

Affiliate disclosure: Links to Amazon on this page are ordinary Amazon.com links. We are not Amazon and are not an authorized Amazon reseller. We may join the Amazon Associates program; if we do, qualifying links will carry a tracking tag and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you, and our disclosure page will say so. Our picks and wording are not paid for. Prices and specs change; the Amazon listing is the source of truth.

A Kindle sleeve is the simplest protection you can buy: a padded pouch that the Kindle slides into and out of, with nothing attached to the device itself. It is also the accessory most often bought on a size label that turns out to mean little. "Fits 6-inch Kindles" describes the screen, not the pouch, and the difference between a sleeve that fits and one that is a struggle can be a few millimeters. This page compares sleeves with cases and folio covers, lines up published Kindle dimensions — including the 2026 Paperwhite — against the interior sizes sellers state, and explains when a sleeve is the right answer.

The short answer

  • Choose a Kindle sleeve if your Kindle spends its time in a bag and you read it bare, or if you already use a case and want a second layer for travel.
  • Choose a case or folio cover instead if you want something on the device while you read: a flap that wakes it, grip, a stand or a strap. See the Kindle case buying guide, the Kindle Paperwhite cover guide and the Paperwhite case fit guide.
  • Size by numbers, not by the screen label. Compare the device's outer size (below) with the sleeve's stated interior size and leave some margin. The 2026 Paperwhite is 126.8 × 174.7 × 6.8 mm (secondary sources).
  • Own a Scribe or Oasis? Different footprint from a Paperwhite — see the size table. Scribe owners: also see the Scribe case guide.
On this page

Sleeve vs case and folio cover

A sleeve and a case solve different problems. A case or folio cover becomes part of the Kindle: it changes how you hold it, how it sleeps and how it charges. A sleeve is a container: it protects the device when it is not in use and then gets out of the way. That is why a sleeve is not a substitute for a folio for most readers, and why it can be the better choice for some.

General comparison. Individual products vary; this is our reasoning, not test results.
SleeveCase or folio cover
When you are readingTakes the Kindle out; no protection while in useOn the device the whole time; adds grip, maybe a stand
In a bagProtects against scratches and knocks; screen is insideFolios cover the screen; shells do not
Fit to modelLooser; can fit several Kindles if the interior is large enoughTight; must match the model year
Auto wake/sleepNoneUsually, on folios
Weight and bulkIn the bag, not on the deviceAdds weight to the device itself
ChargingTake it out to chargeMay need a cutout; dock limits apply
ReusabilityOften carries over when you upgrade, if the size still fitsUsually has to be replaced with each new model

That last row is the sleeve's real advantage. Cases are cut to the exact model year; Amazon's own 2024 fabric cover is listed as fitting the 2024 release only, and its 2026 knit cover names 2026 Paperwhite and Colorsoft only. A sleeve with some slack might carry on through an upgrade, as long as you check the numbers. For the case and cover side of this decision, see our Paperwhite case guide and the Kindle Paperwhite cover guide.

Sleeve sizes by Kindle model

These are the published outer dimensions of the models most people own. They are the numbers to compare against a sleeve's interior. All are from Amazon's listings or press coverage, except where marked. Refreshed October 19, 2026.

The outliers are the Oasis, which is short but wide (159 × 141 mm), so its width is the number to check, and the Scribe, which is a much larger device. A "6-7 inch" sleeve is not going to fit a Scribe and is not meant to.

2026 Paperwhite dimensions — source note

The 126.8 × 174.7 × 6.8 mm figures come from secondary write-ups (Xataka, Case Society Co, Read with Pro) that cite Amazon product data. We have not pulled them from a live Amazon US technical card ourselves, and we have not measured a sleeve against a 2026 device. US buyer reports will not exist until after the October 28, 2026 ship date.

Reading the interior size

A sleeve listing usually gives an external size and an internal size. The external size tells you how much room it takes in your bag; the internal size tells you whether the Kindle fits. The numbers in listings are not always reliable, and at least one seller states that its sizes were measured by hand and "there will be some deviation." Here is what the listings we looked at say, set against the 2024 Paperwhite (still the best-documented reference; the 2026 model is a few millimeters smaller):

Interior sizes as stated by sellers on Amazon.com listings we checked; margins are our own arithmetic against a 176.7 × 127.6 mm device, not tested fit.
Sleeve (type, as listed)Stated interiorSpare length / width vs 2024 PaperwhiteComment
MoKo 6-7 inch, padded, dual pockets and pen loop7.87 × 5.9 in (about 200 × 150 mm)About 23 mm / 22 mmNames 6.8-inch Paperwhite 2021, Oasis and many older Kindles; roomy.
MoKo 6-7 inch, nylon, dual pockets7.48 × 5.51 × 0.59 in (19 × 14 × 1.5 cm)About 13 mm / 12 mmNames the Paperwhite 2021 and the Colorsoft Signature Edition (2024); snugger, with 15 mm of depth.
kwmobile 6-inch neoprene pouch6.7 × 4.7 × 0.8 in (17 × 12 × 2 cm)Negative: shorter than the deviceA reviewer calls it too tight for even the 2018 Paperwhite (167 × 116 mm).

Two rules of thumb follow from the arithmetic, though neither is a tested guarantee. First, you want at least a centimeter of spare length so you can slide the Kindle in and out without a fight, and a few millimeters of spare width. Second, depth matters when you add a case or screen protector; the nylon sleeve's stated depth of 15 mm is plenty for a bare Kindle but modest for a thick folio. And if the Oasis is yours, note that the 141 mm width is just over the nylon sleeve's stated 140 mm interior, so for that model the roomier sleeve is the safer bet (we did not find a listing that gives Oasis-specific interior numbers).

Search Amazon: Kindle sleeve

Example styles (illustrative)

One cleaned example of a soft flap sleeve. Dimensions on marketplace size charts are seller-stated; compare them to your Kindle’s outer size and leave margin.

Materials

General trade-offs from how sellers describe their products, not test results.
MaterialWhat sellers sayTrade-off
NeopreneThe kwmobile pouch listing describes a lightweight, water-resistant neoprene and elastane mix with a zipper.Stretchy and slim, but the stretch is limited; the size label is the thing to check. Often has no pockets.
Nylon with flannel liningMoKo describes a water-resistant nylon exterior, flannel lining and a sealed zipper.Light and wipeable; lining quality varies.
Padded polyesterMoKo describes an "anti-splash" polyester exterior, soft lining and thick padding.More padding for knocks; also more bulk.
Felt, canvas and leatherOther styles exist; we did not check specific listings.Leather and felt look good and age well; protect less from splashes.

Padding and lining matter more than the outer fabric. A good sleeve is soft on the inside so that it does not scratch the screen, and padded enough that a knock in a bag is cushioned. Neither of those is visible in photos, so read the reviews that mention scratches and fit. Be wary of sleeves that rely on a thin, non-padded lining for a Kindle going into a crowded backpack.

Features worth having

  • Zipper vs open top. Zippers keep the Kindle inside if the bag is turned over. Open-top sleeves are faster but can let it slide out.
  • Accessory pockets. The MoKo listings above mention inner pockets for chargers, a power bank, pens or earphones, and an elastic pen loop. Useful if you want a tidy tech pouch; it also adds bulk.
  • Wrist strap or handle. Some pouches have a strap; helpful for hand carry.
  • Exterior pocket. A place for a notepad or the dock cable.
  • Pen holder for the Scribe. The Scribe's pen clings to the device with a magnet, and a bag is a good place to lose it. MoKo's Scribe sleeve listing includes an elastic pen holder.

When a sleeve is the right choice

Our reasoning, not test results.
SituationSleeve?Why
You carry the Kindle in a backpack or tote with other thingsYesKeeps keys and cables from scratching the screen.
You hate cases and read bareYesProtection in transit, nothing on the device in the hand.
You commute or fly and want a second layerYes, with a slim caseA sleeve outside the case; check depth.
You read one-handed in bed and want gripNot aloneA sleeve does nothing while you read; see the cover guide.
You want the Kindle to wake when you open a flapNoThat is a folio cover feature.
You buy for a childProbably not aloneKids models come with a cover; see the case guide.

Using a sleeve and a case together

It is a common combination, and it works if the numbers add up. Add the case's thickness to the Kindle's (7.8 mm for the 2024 Paperwhite; 6.8 mm for the 2026), then compare with the sleeve's interior depth. If the case is a hard back with a flap, the sleeve's depth and its zipper clearance are the limiting factors, not the length. If you do not know the cased dimensions, measure them yourself with a ruler; sellers' sizes are approximate. A sleeve that is too tight on a cased Kindle can strain the cover's flap. If that is a concern, choose a sleeve marked for a larger tablet (8-inch rather than 6-7 inch), and accept that it will leave more slack. For Paperwhite-year fit on the case itself, see Paperwhite cases; for stand and dock notes, see the stand guide.

Listing red flags

  • "6-inch" with no interior dimensions. That describes the screen, not the pouch.
  • A giant compatibility list including phones, tablets and several Kindles; the list may be generous. Check the interior numbers yourself.
  • Interior size missing or in only one unit. Look for both external and internal numbers.
  • Reviews saying "tight" or "too small" for a model like yours. Search the reviews for your model's name.
  • "Waterproof" wording without a rating. We have not seen a recognized rating on any sleeve listing we checked.
  • Words suggesting Amazon approval. Third-party sleeves are third-party. We found no Amazon-branded sleeve while preparing this page, which is not proof there is none; check the Amazon listing.

How we researched this

This guide uses Amazon and retailer listings for the sleeves named (MoKo and kwmobile), Amazon device specifications and spec tables, and press coverage from WIRED, Engadget, The Verge and Digital Trends. We refreshed 2026 Paperwhite outer dimensions on October 19, 2026 against secondary reports of Amazon product data. Sleeve brands are named only because their listings gave interior dimensions we could use as examples; we are not recommending or ranking them, and we have not tested any. Interior sizes are as stated by sellers and may differ from real life. Margins are our arithmetic. To report a mistake, use our contact page; see also our editorial policy.

  • Amazon.com listings for MoKo 6-7 inch Kindle sleeves (padded and nylon versions) and a kwmobile 6-inch neoprene pouch: stated sizes, compatibility lists, materials; checked October 2026.
  • MoKo's Kindle Scribe 10.2-inch sleeve listing (Amazon.ca): interior size, pen holder.
  • Amazon device listings and spec tables: 2022/2024 Kindle, 2024 Paperwhite and Colorsoft Signature Edition, 2018 Paperwhite, Oasis 10th generation.
  • Xataka, Case Society Co, Read with Pro (Oct 2026): 2026 Paperwhite 126.8 × 174.7 × 6.8 mm and Signature ~229 g, citing Amazon product data (secondary; not Amazon US tech card pulled by us).
  • WIRED, Engadget and The Verge (Oct 1, 2026): 2026 Kindle and Paperwhite thickness and weight; power button move.
  • Digital Trends review of the 2024 Kindle: same size as 2022.

Frequently asked questions

Is a Kindle sleeve enough, or do I need a case?

A sleeve is enough if the Kindle mostly rides in a bag and you read it bare. It guards against scratches from keys and charger cables and softens light knocks, but it does nothing while you are reading. If you want something on the device while you read it (grip, a stand, a cover that wakes it), you want a case or folio cover. Many people use both: a slim case in the hand and a sleeve in the bag. See the Kindle case buying guide and the Kindle Paperwhite cover guide.

How do I match a Kindle sleeve to my Paperwhite size?

Compare the device's outer size with the sleeve's stated interior size and leave some margin (about a centimeter of spare length helps). The 2024 Paperwhite is 176.7 × 127.6 × 7.8 mm; the 2026 Paperwhite is 174.7 × 126.8 × 6.8 mm (secondary sources citing Amazon product data — see the size table). Two Amazon listings for "6-7 inch" sleeves state interiors of about 200 × 150 mm and 190 × 140 mm, which leave spare length by our arithmetic. A "6-inch" pouch with a 170 × 120 mm interior is shorter than either Paperwhite.

Will a sleeve made for a 6-inch Kindle fit a Paperwhite?

Not necessarily. A 6-inch label describes the screen, not the pouch. One neoprene "6-inch" pouch lists an interior of 6.7 × 4.7 in (170 × 120 mm), and a reviewer on that listing says it is a tight fit even for the 2018 Paperwhite, which is 167 × 116 mm. The 2021, 2024 and 2026 Paperwhites have a 7-inch (6.8-inch on the 2021 model) screen and are larger than that. Choose a sleeve that states 6-7 inch compatibility, or better, one that names your model and lists interior dimensions.

Sleeve vs folio cover: when is each enough?

A folio cover stays on while you read, protects the screen when closed, and usually adds auto wake/sleep; it must match your model year. A sleeve protects only in a bag and then gets out of the way, so it adds nothing in your hand and can often outlast a device upgrade if the interior still fits. If you hate cases and only need bag protection, a sleeve is enough. If you toss the Kindle into a backpack and also want a flap while reading, use both — or pick a folio and skip the sleeve. Details: sleeve vs case and the cover types page.

Can I put a Kindle that is already in a case into a sleeve?

Only if the sleeve is large enough for the device and the case together. Add the case's thickness and the folded flap to the device's outer size, then compare with the sleeve's interior width, height and depth. A padded sleeve with an interior depth of about 15 mm (as one nylon listing states) leaves modest room beyond a bare 7–8 mm Kindle. A thick folio may not fit. If you use both, buy the sleeve for the cased size, or pick one marked for a larger tablet.

Will a sleeve fit the 2026 Kindle and Paperwhite?

Thickness is unlikely to be the problem: both 2026 models are 6.8 mm thick (WIRED / Engadget). For the Paperwhite, secondary sources cite Amazon product data at 126.8 × 174.7 × 6.8 mm — slightly smaller in footprint than the 2024 model — so a "6-7 inch" sleeve that already fits a 2024 Paperwhite should have room, but we have not measured any sleeve against a 2026 device. One UK retailer lists the base Kindle at 152.7 × 107.9 × 6.8 mm; we could not confirm that against Amazon US. Leave margin and check the sleeve's stated interior.

Do Scribe and Oasis need different sleeve sizes than a Paperwhite?

Yes. The Oasis (10th gen) is short but wide at 159 × 141 mm, so its width is the number to check against a sleeve interior. The Scribe is a much larger device: 230 × 196 mm for the 2022/2024 models and 245 × 189 mm for the 2025 / Colorsoft Scribe. A "6-7 inch" Paperwhite sleeve will not fit a Scribe. See the size table and the Scribe case guide.

Does a sleeve protect against water?

Only as far as the seller says, and the claims differ. One nylon listing calls its exterior water-resistant and its zipper sealed, another describes anti-splash polyester, and a neoprene pouch listing calls its material water-resistant. None of that is a waterproof rating, and none replaces the Kindle's own rating (the 2024 and — per Amazon UK — 2026 Paperwhite are IPX8; the basic Kindle is not waterproof). Treat a sleeve as protection from drizzle and spills in a bag, not from submersion.

What sleeve works for a Kindle Scribe?

Scribe sleeves are scarcer, and the sizes differ by model year. One MoKo sleeve for the 10.2-inch Scribe (2022 and 2024) states an interior of 9.84 × 8.66 in (about 250 × 220 mm) and has an elastic pen holder. The 2022 and 2024 Scribes are 230 × 196 mm; the 2025 Scribe is 245 × 189 mm. We did not find a sleeve listing for the 2025 model to check, and the sleeve will not keep the pen magnetically attached. See the Scribe case styles and verify inner dimensions yourself.

Does it matter if my Kindle wakes up inside the sleeve?

A little. A sleeve has no magnet to put the Kindle to sleep, so it relies on the Kindle's own screen timeout, and a tight pouch could press the power button or touch the screen. We have no test of this, and the pressure depends on the fit and the model (the 2026 models move the power button to the right edge near the top, per The Verge). If it worries you, put the Kindle to sleep yourself before packing it, and choose a sleeve that is not too snug.

Kindle Stand Guide: How to Choose a Desk, Bed or Charging Stand

Facts checked October 5, 2026. Independent guide based on Amazon's announcements and listings plus press coverage. We have not hands-on tested any stand and do not rank products.

Affiliate disclosure: Links to Amazon on this page are ordinary Amazon.com links. We are not Amazon and are not an authorized Amazon reseller. We may join the Amazon Associates program; if we do, qualifying links will carry a tracking tag and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you, and our disclosure page will say so. Our picks and wording are not paid for. Prices and specs change; the Amazon listing is the source of truth.

A Kindle is light enough to hold in one hand, so a stand is not about carrying the weight. It is about not having to hold anything: reading on a desk while you eat, in bed without your arms going numb, on a tray table, or a Kindle that stays upright and charged on a nightstand. This guide sorts the kinds of stand, explains what makes one steady and what does not, and answers the question most shoppers miss: whether the stand works with your case and your model.

The short answer

  • Reading at a desk or table: a weighted stand with adjustable tilt (and ideally height) is the usual choice.
  • Reading in bed hands-free: a clamp-on gooseneck if you have a sturdy headboard or frame, or a lap pillow with a holder if you do not. Consider a Bluetooth page-turn remote.
  • Keeping a Signature Edition upright and charged: a charging dock, but only one listed for your exact model. Amazon's docks are model-specific.
  • Propping it occasionally: a folio cover with a stand mode may be all you need; see the cover types guide.
  • Before you buy: check weight rating, how the stand holds the device (clamp, lip or ledge), whether your case fits, and for a Scribe, whether it is rated for a larger device.

Desk and table stands

This is the largest category on Amazon, and most of it is not made for Kindles at all: general tablet and phone stands that list a range of screen sizes and happen to hold a Kindle. That is fine, because a Kindle is a light, small device. What matters is the stand, not the label.

As an example of what the specifications look like, a Baseus adjustable tablet stand listing that we looked at (it showed as unavailable when we checked, so this is not a recommendation) states compatibility with screens from 5.5 to 21.5 inches, height adjustment from 10.62 to 13.77 inches, a tilt range of 10 to 45 degrees, aluminum alloy construction, a 500 g weighted base and a hinge rated for up to 3.30 lb. Customers on that listing are split: some call it sturdy, others say it is not. That mix is typical, and a reason to read recent reviews that mention stability and use the specifications as a checklist rather than a verdict.

If you only want a simple support that keeps a Kindle at a fixed reading angle, a small foldable stand does the job at a lower price and takes little space. It is also easier to pack, which matters if you read on the go.

Search Amazon: Kindle desk stands

Bed, couch and lap stands

Reading in bed is where most people want a stand, and also where most stands struggle, because a mattress is not a table. There are three common answers.

  • Clamp-on gooseneck holders. A flexible arm clamps to a headboard, bed frame or table edge and holds the Kindle in front of you. A listing we saw states compatibility with devices of 4.7 to 8.6 inches, which covers a Kindle or Paperwhite but not a Scribe. The practical limits are the clamp point (it must be sturdy and the right thickness) and the arm itself: a longer flexible arm sways more when you tap the screen.
  • Lap or bed pillows with a holder. A weighted pillow with a built-in cradle for the device. One lifestyle review we read describes a pillow-with-snack-compartment design that sits on the lap; it is promotional in tone and anecdotal, so treat it as a description of the category and not evidence that any product works. Pillow stands move with you, which is the appeal, but their angle depends on how you sit.
  • Floor stands. A tall stand with a heavy base that lets you read lying down. Stable, but big, and mostly built for larger tablets.

For all three, think about how you turn pages. If you cannot reach the screen without moving, a stand that holds the Kindle out of reach is frustrating. The usual fix is a remote, covered under hands-free reading.

Charging docks

A charging dock is a stand with a purpose, and it is the only type that does not work with every Kindle. Amazon's Wireless Charging Dock for the Paperwhite Signature Editions (2022 and 2024 releases) and the Colorsoft Signature Edition (2024) lists these details on Amazon.com:

  • Portrait orientation: the Kindle sits upright on the dock's ledge.
  • Charges with a case up to 4 mm thick.
  • Up to 7.5 W; Amazon says 100% in as little as 2.5 hours.
  • An LED that blinks when the Kindle is not properly aligned and stays steady when charging or full.
  • Compatible only with the Signature Edition models named in the title. It is not for the standard Paperwhite or the basic Kindle.
  • $44.99 on the listing when we checked on October 5, 2026.

Customer experience on that listing is mixed: many reviewers like it, but a sizeable group reports it failing to charge or flashing without charging, and some mention a case that was too thick. That is not a test, only a reminder that wireless charging depends on alignment and on what is between the coils.

For the 2026 generation, Amazon's announcement lists a $59.99 Charging Dock for the Paperwhite Signature Edition and Colorsoft Signature Edition that keeps them upright and charged. The Signature Editions use pogo pins on the rear for dock charging and for Amazon's $79.99 Page-Turn Cover, so a case that covers the pins can block both. The sources we found do not say whether the 2026 dock works with the 2024 Signature Edition or vice versa, so do not assume either. Our Paperwhite case guide explains the Signature Edition and charging in more detail, and our Kindle charger guide covers cables, adapters and wireless charging for every model.

Built-in cover stands

Many folio covers fold back into a stand at one or two angles. Amazon's 2025 Scribe folio listing, for example, mentions low and high stand angles. The advantage is that it costs nothing extra and travels with the Kindle. The limits are that it only works with that cover on, you do not choose the angle precisely, and on a Scribe, a stand fold can put magnets close to the writing area, which some reviewers report as interfering with the pen (anecdotal). Our cover types guide covers folio constructions, and the Kindle case buying guide includes a stand-style row in its comparison of case styles.

Going fully hands-free

A stand holds the Kindle; it does not turn the page. Amazon's 2026 announcement says exactly that about its own setup: "we've watched Kindle fans engineer their own reading setups for years—propping devices on pillows, rigging phone stands as makeshift docks, and hunting for the easiest possible page turn." Its answer is the Kindle Click, a $34.99 Bluetooth remote that Amazon describes as ideal for reading under the covers, on a treadmill or on a tray table, and compatible with all new Kindle devices and any Kindle from 2024 or later. For the Signature Editions, there is also the $79.99 Page-Turn Cover with physical buttons. We have not tested either.

If your Kindle is older than 2024, we did not find Amazon support for the Click, so a stand that lets you reach the screen is the safer plan. Our Kindle page turner guide compares the Click, the Page-Turn Cover, clip-on tappers and Double Tap by model.

Listing red flags

  • "Compatible with all Kindles" and a charging function in the same listing. Chargers are model-specific.
  • No weight rating on a tall or arm-style stand.
  • Reviews that say it tips, droops or slides on beds or soft surfaces. Sort by recent and search "tips," "wobble," "droops," "slides."
  • A clamp range that does not match your headboard or frame. Measure it.
  • A device-size range that stops short of the Scribe if you own one.
  • Claims of Amazon approval on a third-party stand. We do not use that language here either.
  • Unusually low prices on a charging dock that claims to match Amazon's. Check the title for your exact model.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a stand, or is a folio cover with a stand mode enough?

A folio that folds into a stand is enough for a tray table or a short read, and it costs nothing extra if you already own one. A dedicated stand gives more control over angle and height, keeps the Kindle off your lap and can stay put while you swap covers. If you mostly read at a desk or in bed, a separate stand is usually steadier. See the cover features section for what a built-in stand involves.

Will a Kindle stand work with my case on?

Check two things: the opening or clamp width, and the thickness the stand allows. Amazon's wireless charging dock, for example, says it works with a case up to 4 mm thick, and the user reviews on that listing are mixed about charging with a case on. Clamp-style holders list a device-size range, which is not the same as a thickness limit, so read the listing for it. A slim shell or no case is the safest pairing; a thick folio often has to be folded back or removed.

Do I need a stand that is specific to a Kindle?

No. Most Kindle stands are general tablet or phone holders. What you need is a stand that handles the device's size and weight: about 140 to 219 g for the Kindles with 6- to 7-inch screens (158 g for the 2022 and 2024 basic Kindle, 211 g for the 2024 Paperwhite, 219 g for the Colorsoft Signature Edition, and WIRED reports 204 g for the 2026 Paperwhite), and about 400 to 433 g for the Scribe. Charging docks are the exception: Amazon's are made for specific Signature Edition models only.

Which charging dock works with which Kindle?

Amazon's wireless charging dock is listed for the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Editions (2022 and 2024) and the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (2024) only. Amazon's October 1, 2026 announcement lists a $59.99 charging dock for the 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition and Colorsoft Signature Edition, with pogo pin charging. We did not find a statement on whether either dock works with the other generation, or with standard Paperwhites or the basic Kindle, so check the listing for your exact model.

Is a gooseneck holder good for reading in bed?

It can be, if you have a headboard, bed frame or table edge to clamp to. The appeal is that the arm holds the Kindle in front of you without your hands. The trade-off is that a long flexible arm can sway when you tap, and a clamp needs a sturdy place to grip. Pairing a hands-free holder with a Bluetooth remote such as Amazon's $34.99 Kindle Click (which Amazon says works with all new Kindles and any Kindle from 2024 or later) means you do not have to touch the screen at all.

What angle should a Kindle stand hold?

There is no single right angle, and we have no test data. Reading is usually most comfortable when the screen is facing you rather than looking down at it, so a stand with a tilt range and some height adjustment gives you room to find a spot. One tablet-stand listing we checked states a tilt range of 10 to 45 degrees; another type, the pillow stand, usually holds a set angle that changes with how your lap is positioned. Choose adjustability if you read in more than one position.

Is a heavy base really important?

For a tall desk stand, yes, reasonably so: a light base on a bed or an armchair tray can tip when you tap the screen. One adjustable tablet stand we looked at lists a 500 g weighted base and says its hinge bears up to 3.3 lb, yet reviewers on that listing are split on how steady it is, so the number alone is not a guarantee. A Kindle is lighter than a tablet, which helps, but the stand's footprint and friction still matter. Check recent reviews that mention stability.

Can I use a Kindle stand for the Scribe?

Only if it is rated for the Scribe's size and weight. The Scribe is 10.2 or 11 inches and weighs 400 to 433 g, and many "Kindle" holders are sized for 6- to 8-inch devices. The pen also clings to the side of the device by a magnet, so a clamp or a tight cradle can bump or hide it. For writing, you may want to lay the Scribe flat or on a low-angle stand rather than upright. Our Scribe case guide covers the pen and magnets.

Kindle Colorsoft Case: Which One Fits Your Colorsoft

Facts checked October 5, 2026. Independent guide based on Amazon's listings, user guides and announcements plus press coverage. We have not hands-on tested any case mentioned.

Affiliate disclosure: Links to Amazon on this page are ordinary Amazon.com links. We are not Amazon and are not an authorized Amazon reseller. We may join the Amazon Associates program; if we do, qualifying links will carry a tracking tag and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you, and our disclosure page will say so. Our picks and wording are not paid for. Prices and specs change; the Amazon listing is the source of truth.

"Kindle Colorsoft" now covers four different devices: the original 2024 Signature Edition, a cheaper 16 GB model from 2025, a redesigned 2026 Colorsoft that ships at the end of October, and the much larger Kindle Scribe Colorsoft. A case that fits one may not fit the next. This guide sorts out which Colorsoft you have, which cases are made for it, and the few things about a color Kindle that change what to look for in a case, such as Double Tap, wireless charging and the pogo pins on the 2026 Signature Edition.

Short answer

  • 2024 Colorsoft Signature Edition or 2025 Colorsoft 16 GB: look for cases that name the Colorsoft. Amazon gives the 2024 Colorsoft the same outer size as the 2024 Paperwhite, and Amazon's own case is listed for both, so 2024 Paperwhite cases that also name the Colorsoft are the usual choice.
  • 2026 Colorsoft: a thinner new body (6.8 mm) with the power button moved to the right edge. Do not reuse a 2024 case. Wait for listings that name the 2026 model, or start with Amazon's 2026 covers.
  • Kindle Scribe Colorsoft (11-inch): a different device entirely. Use the Scribe case guide.
  • Signature Edition owners: check that the case keeps Double Tap working, and that it suits wireless charging (2024) or leaves the pogo pins clear (2026).

Which Colorsoft do you have?

Start here, because the name alone does not tell a case seller which body you own.

  • 7-inch, power button on the bottom edge, launched 2024: the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition. Amazon's listing calls it "Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (1st Generation) – 2024 release." It has 32 GB, an auto-adjusting front light and Qi wireless charging.
  • The same shape, 16 GB, launched July 24, 2025: the Kindle Colorsoft 16 GB. Amazon's announcement says the Signature Edition adds an auto-adjusting front light, wireless charging and 32 GB over it. The Kindle Colorsoft Kids launched the same day with its own kid-friendly cover included.
  • 7-inch with the power button on the right edge, near the top: the 2026 Kindle Colorsoft or Colorsoft Signature Edition, announced October 1, 2026 and shipping October 28. The Verge reports the button moved across the new lineup; the Signature Edition has an aluminum back with pogo pins.
  • 11-inch with a pen: the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft (2025). See the Scribe Colorsoft section.

To confirm, the Kindle's Device Info screen in settings shows the device's name and generation, according to Amazon's user guides, and so does your device list in your Amazon account. The release year is the safer matching key than any generation number.

Second, the 2024 Colorsoft weighs 8 g more than the 2024 Paperwhite (219 g against 211 g, both Amazon figures), which does not change the fit of a case made for the shared body.

2024 and 2025 Colorsoft cases

For the 2024 Signature Edition, the fit question is simpler than it looks. Amazon gives exactly the same outer dimensions for it and for the 2024 Paperwhite, 127.6 × 176.7 × 7.8 mm, and Amazon's plant-based leather case says it is "compatible with Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (Fits 2024 Release Only), Kindle Colorsoft and Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition." Third-party accessory makers group them the same way: for example, a tempered-glass screen protector sold at Best Buy is titled for the "Kindle Paperwhite 2024 and Colorsoft." That is why our 2024 Paperwhite case section notes that many 2024 listings also name the Colorsoft.

Our advice still is to buy a case whose title names the Colorsoft, not just "Paperwhite." Same outer dimensions do not guarantee that a seller has checked the cutouts, the magnet position for auto sleep/wake, or the fit around the Signature Edition's features. Recent reviews from Colorsoft owners, searched for "Colorsoft," "fit" and "button," are the best check we know of.

The 2025 Colorsoft 16 GB is where we have less to go on. Amazon's case listing names the "Kindle Colorsoft" as well as the Signature Edition, and Amazon's announcement describes the difference from the Signature Edition in features (front light, wireless charging, storage) rather than size, but we did not find a separate dimension listing for it. Treat a case that names both as the safe choice.

What about older Paperwhite cases? A 2021 Paperwhite case will not do: the 2021 model is a 6.8-inch body of about 124.6 × 174 × 8.1 mm in our Paperwhite case guide, smaller than the Colorsoft.

2026 Colorsoft cases

Amazon announced a redesigned Colorsoft on October 1, 2026: a 16 GB model at $289.99 in Graphite and a Signature Edition at $319.99 in Graphite and Fig, with an aluminum housing, 32 GB, an auto-adjusting front light, Double Tap and pogo-pin dock charging. WIRED gives both the Paperwhite and the Colorsoft as 6.8 mm thick and 204 g. Pre-orders open on a rolling basis and the devices ship October 28, 2026.

For cases, that adds up to a new body. It is a full millimeter thinner than the 2024 Colorsoft, The Verge reports the power button moved from the bottom to the right edge near the top, and Amazon describes a flush-front display with color that "wraps seamlessly from front to back." A 2024 case would at best be loose and at worst cover the button, so do not reuse one.

  • Amazon's 2026 covers: Kindle Covers from $39.99 in knit fabric, plant-based leather and pebbled premium leather that "wrap fully around the device," color-matched across the lineup.
  • Slim magnetic-attach covers: Amazon says these are also available for devices with aluminum housing, which includes the Colorsoft Signature Edition. Our cover guide explains the magnetic-attach trade-off.
  • Page-Turn Cover ($79.99): a magnetic cover with physical page-turn buttons that connects through the pogo pins, for the Paperwhite and Colorsoft Signature Editions.
  • Third-party: at our check the 2026 Colorsoft had not shipped, so any third-party listing for it was made before owners could test fit. Look for reviews from owners after October 28.

What a color screen changes about choosing a case

Less than you might expect. We looked for anything Amazon or independent reviewers say about cases and color displays specifically, and here is what we found, and did not find.

So the color screen itself is not a reason to pick a different case. The real Colorsoft-specific factors are the Signature Edition features in the next section. If you are weighing a screen protector, our screen protector notes apply to the shared 2024 body, with the added unknown of how a protector interacts with the color filter layer, which we could not verify.

Signature Edition features and cases

These are the features where a case can get in the way, by model.

  • Double Tap (2024 and 2026 Signature Editions). Amazon's 2024 Colorsoft guide describes accelerometer-based tap detection: tap twice quickly on the side or back, outside the screen, to go forward. It adds that the feature "has been tested with the official Amazon Kindle Colorsoft case, but may not work with all third party cases." If you rely on it, that is a reason to start with Amazon's case or to test a third-party case within its return window. Our page turner guide covers the feature.
  • Qi wireless charging (2024 Signature Edition). The user guide says it charges on "any compatible Qi-certified wireless charger," then lists ten Qi-certified chargers that do not work with it because of "mechanical incompatibility." Amazon's wireless dock for it states a 4 mm case limit, and Amazon's safety text says to keep metallic or magnetic objects, including metallic cases, off the charger. A thin, non-metal case is the safest pairing.
  • Pogo pins (2026 Signature Edition). The contacts on the back connect to Amazon's $59.99 Charging Dock and the $79.99 Page-Turn Cover. A case that covers them blocks both. Notebookcheck reported that the dock had no release date at launch, while the Page-Turn Cover ships October 28.
  • USB-C (2024 and 2025 models; 2026 Signature Edition per The Verge). Amazon's plant-based case can stay on while charging. For third-party cases, check the cutout. Our Kindle charger guide lists Amazon's charge times and adapters for the Colorsoft.

The 16 GB models have none of the first three, so for them the choice is about fit, style and the USB-C cutout.

Kindle Scribe Colorsoft

The Scribe Colorsoft shares the Colorsoft name and display technology but not the size: it is an 11-inch writing tablet at 189 × 245 × 5.4 mm and 400 g by Amazon's figures, with the Premium Pen attached magnetically to the right side. Its cases are Scribe cases, with pen loops or flaps and attention to the pen magnet, and Amazon's listing says it charges in less than 3 hours with a 20W USB-C adapter. We cover it model by model, including what we could not confirm about whether it shares cases with the 2025 black-and-white Scribe, in the Kindle Scribe case guide, so we do not repeat it here.

Search Amazon: Scribe Colorsoft cases

Colorsoft case red flags

  • "Colorsoft case" with no screen size. It may be for the 11-inch Scribe Colorsoft.
  • One listing for "all Colorsoft" spanning 2024 and 2026. The 2026 body is thinner with the button in a different place.
  • Only "Paperwhite" in the title. A 2024 Paperwhite case may fit, but a listing that names the Colorsoft is safer, and a 2021 or 2026 Paperwhite case will not.
  • Metal plates or strong magnets in the back if you charge a 2024 Signature Edition wirelessly.
  • Coverage over the pogo pins on a 2026 Signature Edition if you want the dock or Page-Turn Cover.
  • "Official" or "Amazon certified" on a non-Amazon product. We cannot verify it and do not use that language ourselves.

How we researched this

This guide uses Amazon.com listings for the 2024 Colorsoft Signature Edition, the 2024 Paperwhite, the Scribe Colorsoft and Amazon's plant-based leather case; Amazon's 2024 Colorsoft user guide; Amazon's July 2025 Colorsoft announcement and its October 1, 2026 lineup announcement; and coverage from The Verge and WIRED. We have not tested any case, and we do not rank third-party products. Prices and ratings are snapshots from October 5, 2026. Where a detail is unpublished, such as the 2026 Colorsoft's width and height, we say so. To report a mistake, use our contact page; our approach is described in the editorial policy.

Frequently asked questions

Do Kindle Paperwhite cases fit the Kindle Colorsoft?

A case for the 2024 Paperwhite usually does, and a case for any other Paperwhite does not. Amazon lists identical outer dimensions for the 2024 Paperwhite and the 2024 Colorsoft Signature Edition (127.6 × 176.7 × 7.8 mm), and Amazon's own plant-based leather case is listed for the 2024 Paperwhite, the Colorsoft and the Colorsoft Signature Edition. The 2021 Paperwhite is a smaller 6.8-inch body, and the 2026 Paperwhite and Colorsoft are a new, thinner design. Buy a case whose title names your Colorsoft, not just "Paperwhite."

Will a 2024 Colorsoft case fit the 2026 Colorsoft?

We have no evidence that it will, and two reasons to doubt it. WIRED gives the 2026 Colorsoft as 6.8 mm thick, against Amazon's 7.8 mm for the 2024 model, and The Verge reports that the 2026 models moved the power button from the bottom to the right edge near the top, so the cutouts and the fit differ. We found no published width and height for the 2026 Colorsoft yet. Wait for a listing that names the 2026 model, or start with one of Amazon's 2026 covers.

Is a Kindle Colorsoft case the same as a Kindle Scribe Colorsoft case?

No, and this is the easiest mistake to make. The Kindle Colorsoft is a 7-inch e-reader; the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft is an 11-inch writing tablet at 189 × 245 × 5.4 mm with a magnetic pen on the side. Their cases are not interchangeable. Search results for "Colorsoft case" mix both, so check the screen size in the title. For the Scribe, use our Scribe case guide.

Does a case affect the Colorsoft's color screen?

We found no Amazon statement or independent test saying it does. A folio covers the screen only when it is closed; when open, the case wraps the back and frame. What Amazon does say is that the Colorsoft display adds a color filter layer, so its texture or brightness can look different from a Paperwhite's, and that its covers have a microfiber interior to help protect the screen from scratches. A screen protector is a different matter, and there we found listings but no tests of how one affects color or glare.

Does Double Tap work with a case on?

Amazon's user guide for the 2024 Colorsoft says the Signature Edition's Double Tap feature, which turns the page when you tap the side or back twice, "has been tested with the official Amazon Kindle Colorsoft case, but may not work with all third party cases." A thick or very soft case could plausibly dampen the taps, but we have not tested any. If you use Double Tap, Amazon's case is the one option Amazon says was tested.

Can I wirelessly charge my Colorsoft in a case?

Only the 2024 Colorsoft Signature Edition supports Qi wireless charging; Amazon's 2025 announcement says wireless charging is one of the things the Signature Edition adds over the 16 GB model. Amazon's wireless dock is listed for the "Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (2024 Release)" and states a 4 mm case limit, and Amazon's safety text says to keep metallic or magnetic objects, including metallic cases, off a wireless charger. The 2026 Colorsoft Signature Edition uses a pogo-pin dock instead, so a case must leave the pins on the back clear.

Do the Colorsoft 16 GB and the Signature Edition use the same case?

Amazon's own plant-based leather case lists both the "Kindle Colorsoft" and the "Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition," which suggests a shared body for the 2024 and 2025 models, but we did not find separate published dimensions for the 16 GB model. For the 2026 generation, the Signature Edition has an aluminum back and pogo pins, and Amazon also sells slim magnetic-attach covers for aluminum models, so check that a 2026 case names your exact edition.

How much is Amazon's official Colorsoft case?

When we checked on October 5, 2026, Amazon's plant-based leather case for the 2024 Paperwhite and Colorsoft was listed at $42.99 in Raspberry, with prices varying by color and seller. For the 2026 lineup, Amazon's announcement lists Kindle Covers from $39.99 and the Page-Turn Cover at $79.99 for the Signature Editions. Prices change often; the Amazon listing is the source of truth.

Kindle Charger: Which Cable and Adapter Your Kindle Needs

Facts checked October 5, 2026. Independent guide based on Amazon's user guides, listings and announcements plus press coverage. We have not tested any charger or cable mentioned.

Affiliate disclosure: Links to Amazon on this page are ordinary Amazon.com links. We are not Amazon and are not an authorized Amazon reseller. We may join the Amazon Associates program; if we do, qualifying links will carry a tracking tag and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you, and our disclosure page will say so. Our picks and wording are not paid for. Prices and specs change; the Amazon listing is the source of truth.

A Kindle is one of the few gadgets where the wall adapter is not in the box, and where two different ports are still in use depending on the year you bought it. This guide sorts out the port on each Kindle, what Amazon actually says about adapters and charging time, how wireless and dock charging differ, and what to try when a Kindle will not charge. It sticks to what Amazon documents, and it says so when a detail is not published.

Short answer

  • Port: USB-C on the 2021 Paperwhite and everything newer that we checked (2022 Kindle, 2024 Paperwhite, 2024 Colorsoft, Scribe). Micro-USB on the 2018 Paperwhite, 2019 Kindle, Oasis and Voyage.
  • Adapter: sold separately. Amazon's guides name its 5W adapter for most models, a 9W one for the Colorsoft, and its 2025 Scribe listings name a 20W USB-C adapter. Third-party adapters work, usually more slowly, if they meet safety standards.
  • Wireless: only the 2021 and 2024 Signature Editions (and the 2024 Colorsoft Signature Edition) support Qi. The 2026 Signature Editions use a pogo-pin dock instead. See the dock section of our stand guide.
  • Case on: check the port cutout, and for wireless charging the case thickness. Our case buying guide covers that.

Charging port by Kindle model

The first question is the port, because it decides the cable. Amazon's user guides use the labels "USB-C/power port" and "Micro-USB/power port," so the table below follows those guides where we could find them. Where we relied on something else, the last column says so.

Two things stand out. First, the cutover is the 2021 Paperwhite: on the models we checked, USB-C starts there and micro-USB ends with the 2019 Kindle, the 2019 Oasis and the 2018 Paperwhite. Second, Amazon's statements on the same model sometimes differ in wording: for the 2024 Paperwhite the user guide mentions a 5W adapter and "less than two hours," while the Amazon.com listing says "less than 2.5 hours with a 9W USB power adapter." We report both rather than pick one. If you own a Kindle older than those in the table, such as a Kindle Touch or an early Paperwhite, we did not check its guide, so look at the port itself.

One 2026 detail to keep in mind: the 2026 devices were still pre-order at our check, shipping October 28, 2026, and Amazon's pages did not yet list adapter wattage or charge times. Amazon's Kevin Keith told The Verge the 2026 models have user-replaceable batteries to comply with EU rules (WIRED says the batteries "should be easier to remove and replace"), but that is no guide to what charger you should buy.

Choosing the right cable

Match the cable to the port: a micro-USB cable will not fit a USB-C Kindle and the reverse. The micro-USB connector is tapered and goes in one way up; USB-C is rounded and goes in either way. The most common mistake we can identify from the listings is buying a "Kindle charger" bundle without checking which port it is for, because older listings for micro-USB Kindles are still on sale next to the newer USB-C ones.

  • For micro-USB Kindles (2019 Kindle, 2018 Paperwhite, Oasis, Voyage): a micro-USB cable plus a USB wall adapter. Amazon's 5W adapter listing says it needs a micro-USB cable, which is not included with it.
  • For USB-C Kindles (2021 Paperwhite and newer): a USB-C cable. The box includes one; spares are cheap and plentiful.
  • Data versus charge-only: Amazon's guides say you can use the supplied cable to transfer files to the Kindle from a computer. As a general USB point (not an Amazon statement), some very cheap cables carry power only and cannot transfer files, so if you plan to sideload books, keep the cable that came in the box.
  • Length and fit: a case with a narrow port cutout can stop a thick cable plug from seating fully. Amazon's guide says to make sure the cable is fully inserted if the charge light does not come on, so test it with your case on.

Adapters: what Amazon says about 5W, 9W and 20W

Amazon sells its own adapters, and its documents refer to three:

Amazon-branded adapters named in Amazon's documents. Prices are Amazon.com snapshots from October 2026.

Amazon 9WColorsoft Signature Edition user guide; Amazon.com listings for the 2024 Paperwhite, Colorsoft and Scribe charge timesIts own Amazon.com listing ("9W Official OEM USB Charger") was $19.99 when we checked and has a USB-A port, so a USB-C Kindle needs a USB-A to USB-C cable with it; Amazon's compliance page for the Scribe Colorsoft shows a 9W Amazon adapter model in its energy table
Amazon 20W USB-CAmazon.com listing for the Scribe Colorsoft; the adapter listing says it charges 2025-and-later Scribes in about two hours (the Scribe Colorsoft listing says "less than 3 hours"; both are Amazon figures)Listed at $19.99, cable sold separately, dated September 30, 2025

The takeaway is that Amazon's documented adapter sizes are modest, and that one adapter is not the only option. Amazon's guides do not say a 5W adapter is required, only that it is the figure behind its published charge times. Beyond that, the compliance page for the Scribe Colorsoft is the most specific: it says the power delivered by the charger "must be between min [2.5] Watts required by the radio equipment, and max [15] Watts in order to achieve the maximum charging speed." In plain terms, Amazon's own figure puts the useful ceiling at 15 W for that device, and a minimum of 2.5 W is needed just to run the radios.

Amazon does not say, in anything we found, whether Kindles negotiate USB Power Delivery. Forum users report that high-wattage adapters work fine because the Kindle simply draws what it needs, but that is user experience, not Amazon documentation, and we have not tested it. The safe reading is the one Amazon gives: a compliant adapter from a reputable maker will charge your Kindle, and the wattage on the label is not a reason to expect a dramatic speed-up.

Charging speed and time

Charge times in Amazon's documents are rough "less than" figures, not measurements. A few patterns hold across the guides and listings we read:

  • The adapter beats the computer. Amazon says third-party adapters or a computer's USB port take "less than three hours" on the USB-C Paperwhite and Scribe and "less than four hours" on the 2022 Kindle, "but may take longer depending on the capability of the hardware." For the 2024 Scribe, the listing puts the computer figure at about 7 hours against about 2.5 hours with a 9W adapter.
  • Quoted times are not comparable across devices. The 2025 Scribe Colorsoft listing says "less than 3 hours" with a 20W adapter, the 2024 Scribe listing says about 2.5 hours with a 9W adapter, and the Paperwhite listing says under 2.5 hours with 9W. Each assumes a different adapter, so do not read them as a ranking of the devices.
  • Charge less often than you think. Amazon rates the 2024 Paperwhite at up to 12 weeks and the 2024 Colorsoft at up to 8 weeks, both "based on a half hour of reading per day with wireless off and the light setting at 13." Amazon says battery life varies with use and that Audible streaming over Bluetooth reduces it, and the user guides add that a weak wireless signal increases power use.
  • A sleeping Kindle is cheap. The 2024 Paperwhite guide says the static lockscreen "uses no battery power," so the quickest way to stretch a charge is to let the Kindle sleep rather than keep the screen awake.

Accessories that charge too: Amazon's new Kindle Click remote is rechargeable over USB-C, with the cable and adapter sold separately. If you buy one, a USB-C cable and a spare port on the adapter will cover both. See our Kindle page turner guide.

Third-party chargers and cables

Amazon's safety documents are not hostile to third-party gear. They say the device uses "the USB cable provided and a USB charger or USB port that is compliant with safety standards, such as IEC 62368," and the user guides give charge times for third-party adapters. The safety text for Japanese customers goes further and warns that a power source that does not match, or a third-party accessory, "may result in malfunction, fire, overheating and other problems." In practice that means:

  • Choose by certification, not by price or wattage. Look for a recognized safety mark and a brand that publishes specifications. We do not name third-party winners, because we have not tested any.
  • Avoid unlabeled adapters and listings that make claims they do not explain, such as "ultra-fast Kindle charging" without a wattage or a standard.
  • Keep the original cable for transfers, and buy a spare of the same connector type for the bedside.
  • Do not rely on a low-power port. The Oasis and Kindle guides say a low-powered USB port, such as those on some keyboards and older computers, will not charge the Kindle.

Wireless charging is not a feature of every Kindle, and it changed in 2026. Here is the position as the sources describe it:

That is a good reason to take off a case with a metal plate or a strong magnet in the back before testing wireless charging. We cover the dock hardware, its 7.5 W rating and customer experience in the stand guide.

Charging with a case on

Cases and chargers interact in two places: the port and the coil.

  • Port cutout: every folio or shell should leave the USB-C or micro-USB port accessible. Amazon's plant-based leather case for the Paperwhite and Colorsoft says "it can remain on your Kindle for charging." For other cases, check the listing photos and recent reviews for "charging."
  • Wireless coil: thick cases can stop a Signature Edition from charging on a pad. Amazon's own dock states a 4 mm case limit. The practical test is to try the Kindle in the case on the pad, as Amazon's alignment light tells you whether it caught.
  • Pogo pins (2026 Signature Editions): the contacts on the rear are used by both the dock and Amazon's Page-Turn Cover, so a case that covers them blocks both. See the Paperwhite case guide.
  • Scribe: the USB-C port is at the bottom on the 2025 models, per reviews we cite in the Scribe case guide, so check the cutout against your model year.

For model-specific fit, the Kindle case buying guide and the Colorsoft case guide cover the charging details for their models.

When a Kindle will not charge

The sequence below follows Amazon's user guides and safety pages. It is not a repair guide, and nothing here replaces contacting Amazon.

  1. Look at the indicator. Amazon's guides say a lightning bolt appears on the battery icon at the top of the Home screen while charging, and the indicator light turns amber while charging and green when full.
  2. Seat the cable. The guides say to make sure the USB cable is fully inserted into the Kindle and into the adapter or computer port.
  3. Change the source. Try another USB port or another wall outlet. Avoid low-powered ports, which Amazon says will not charge the Kindle.
  4. Leave USB drive mode. If it is plugged into a computer, eject it from the computer's desktop (or tap Disconnect on the Scribe). It keeps charging, and you can read again.
  5. Remove the case and see if the plug seats, especially with a narrow cutout.
  6. Restart. For a frozen Kindle, Amazon's guides say to hold the power button until the power dialog appears (about 9 seconds in the 2024 Paperwhite guide) and tap Restart, or, if no dialog appears, hold it for 30 seconds or until the LED stops blinking. Amazon's guides are not consistent here: other sections of the same guides, and the Scribe guide, say 15 seconds.
  7. Dry it. If the Kindle or its port is wet, unplug everything and let it dry completely, per Amazon's safety text.
  8. Contact Amazon. Amazon's safety text says that if the Kindle or its battery was dropped and may be damaged, you should not attempt repair and should contact customer service.

If it fails only on one adapter or cable, the fault is probably that accessory. We cannot say whether a particular fault is common, and we cannot diagnose a device for you.

Safe charging habits from Amazon's guides

  • Charge in a well-ventilated area, away from heat sources, as Amazon's safety text advises for the device and its adapter.
  • Do not charge near water or in extremely humid conditions, even on a waterproof model.
  • Keep to the temperature range Amazon lists. The Scribe Colorsoft's compliance page gives an operating range of 0 to 35 °C (32 to 95 °F); check the page for your model.
  • Use a charger or USB port that complies with safety standards, and the cable Amazon supplied or a good match.
  • On wireless chargers, keep metal objects off the pad.
  • Do not try to open the Kindle or replace its battery yourself. Amazon's safety page says the lithium-ion battery should be replaced only by a qualified service provider.

Charger red flags

  • "Fits all Kindles" with no connector named. There are two ports in use.
  • A micro-USB cable listed for a 2021-or-newer Kindle, or the reverse.
  • Wattage claims with no standard or certification behind them.
  • "Official," "Amazon certified" or "Made for Kindle" on a non-Amazon product. We do not use that language on this site either, and we cannot verify any such claim.
  • A wireless pad sold for "all Kindles" when only some Signature Editions support Qi and some pads are known to be incompatible.
  • A dock listed for a 2024 Signature Edition and a 2026 one together without a statement that both work. Amazon's sources do not say whether the 2026 dock works with the 2024 model.

Frequently asked questions

What charger does my Kindle use?

It depends on the model year. In Amazon's own user guides, the 2021 Paperwhite, 2022 Kindle, 2024 Paperwhite, 2024 Colorsoft Signature Edition and the Scribe all use a USB-C port, while the 2018 Paperwhite, 2019 Kindle, Oasis and Voyage use micro-USB. For the 2026 lineup, press coverage says the Signature Editions have a USB-C port; we did not find an explicit port statement for the other 2026 models. See the port table, and check the port on your own device if you are unsure: micro-USB is tapered, USB-C is a rounded oval that goes in either way up.

Does a Kindle come with a charger?

Usually it comes with a cable but not a wall adapter. Amazon's 2024 Paperwhite listing says the box holds the Kindle, a USB-C charging cable and a quick start guide, and its user guides say the Amazon 5W or 9W charger is "sold separately." Amazon's Scribe listings also list a USB-C cable but no adapter. Any USB wall adapter or computer port that meets safety standards can be used, with different charge times, as explained in the adapter section.

Can I use my phone charger on a Kindle?

Amazon's user guides say third-party adapters work: they give "less than three hours" for the USB-C Paperwhite, Scribe and Colorsoft, and "less than four hours" for the 2022 Kindle and the micro-USB models, against "less than two hours" with Amazon's own 5W or 9W adapter in the USB-C guides, "but may take longer depending on the capability of the hardware." (The 2019 Kindle and Voyage guides give "less than four hours" even with a Kindle AC adapter.) Amazon also tells owners to use a charger or USB port that complies with safety standards such as IEC 62368. We have not tested any phone charger with a Kindle. Use a reputable, certified adapter and a cable that matches the port.

Is a higher-wattage charger faster or safer for a Kindle?

Amazon's own figures stop at modest wattages. Its guides name 5W adapters for most models, 9W for the Colorsoft Signature Edition, and its 2025 Scribe listings name a 20W adapter. For the Scribe Colorsoft, Amazon's compliance page says the charger should deliver between 2.5 and 15 W "to achieve the maximum charging speed," which suggests that more power than that is not expected to speed things up. We found no Amazon statement on USB Power Delivery for Kindles, so we cannot say a bigger adapter charges faster. A fast phone or laptop brick is not something Amazon documents, so choose a reputable one and expect Kindle-level speeds.

Can I charge a Kindle from my computer?

Yes, Amazon's guides say you can use the supplied cable to charge from a computer, but it is slower. Amazon's listing for the 2024 Scribe says a full charge takes about 7 hours from a computer against about 2.5 hours with a 9W USB-C adapter. Two cautions from Amazon's guides: a low-powered USB port, such as those on some keyboards and older computers, "will not receive enough power to charge," and a Kindle in USB drive mode cannot be used for reading until you eject it from your computer, after which it keeps charging.

Why is my Kindle not charging?

Start with Amazon's own checks: push the cable fully into the Kindle and the adapter or computer, try a different USB port or wall outlet, and look for the lightning bolt in the battery icon and the indicator light turning amber while charging and green when full. If it is connected to a computer, eject it so it leaves USB drive mode. If the Kindle seems frozen, Amazon's guides say to hold the power button until the power dialog appears (the 2024 Paperwhite guide says about 9 seconds) and tap Restart, and if no dialog appears to hold it for 30 seconds or until the LED stops blinking. Some sections of the same guides, and the Scribe guide, say 15 seconds instead. See the troubleshooting section for the full list.

What charger does the 2026 Kindle, Paperwhite or Colorsoft use?

Amazon's October 1, 2026 announcement says the Signature Edition Paperwhite and Colorsoft add "pogo pin dock charging," and The Verge says those editions also have a USB-C port and, unlike the 2024 Signature Edition, do not support Qi wireless charging. We did not find Amazon's adapter wattage or charge times for the 2026 models; as of October 5, 2026 the Paperwhite and Colorsoft were pre-order, shipping October 28, 2026. Re-check the listing for your model when it ships.

Can I charge a waterproof Kindle if it just got wet?

Not until it is dry. Amazon's safety information says not to charge the device near water or in extremely humid conditions, and that if it gets wet you should carefully unplug all cables without getting your hands wet and let it dry completely before plugging the cables in again, without using a heat source such as a hair dryer or microwave. A waterproof rating describes immersion, not a damp charging port.

Does any Qi wireless charger work with a Kindle?

Only the Signature Editions that support it, and not every Qi pad fits. Amazon's user guides say the 2021 and 2024 Paperwhite Signature Editions and the 2024 Colorsoft Signature Edition support wireless charging with a Qi-certified charger, and the Colorsoft guide lists ten Qi-certified chargers that are not compatible because of "mechanical incompatibility." Amazon's safety page also says to keep metallic or magnetic objects, including metallic cases, off a wireless charger. The standard models do not support it, and neither does the 2026 Signature Edition. See our dock section.
